project.name: deepinfer
project.description: DeepInfer is DeepSeek's high-performance inference framework for large-scale production serving, released open-source as an offline inference engine for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Its control plane carries vLLM lineage, but the execution layer is rewritten around custom TileLang kernels, Attention-DP / balanced-CP / MoE-EP parallelism with no tensor parallelism, DSpark speculative decoding with confidence-scheduled verification, and SWA bounded replay, targeting NVIDIA SM100 GPUs and Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.s: Ascend/NPU backend of the device-memory utility layer: allocates raw NPU memory via aclrtMalloc (bypassing torch's caching allocator) and exports/imports ACL IPC handles so KV-cache buffers can be shared across processes and cards.

k.s: Imports an ACL IPC key as a byte tensor on the NPU, forcing ENABLE_PEER_ACCESS so kernels can reach the memory across cards in CP>1 fan-out; returns nullopt on failure.
Exports an NPU allocation as an IPC key, asserting the 2MB alignment ACL requires and disabling PID validation so another process can import it.
Allocates page-rounded NPU memory with aclrtMalloc (HUGE_FIRST) and wraps it as a 1-D byte tensor whose deleter calls aclrtFree.
Registers alloc_tensor / export_ipc_tensor / import_ipc_tensor into the cuda_utils pybind submodule.

nodes.s: NVIDIA backend of the device-memory utility layer: allocates device memory through the CUDA driver API (cuMemAlloc) rather than torch's caching allocator, and wraps cudaIpc* so KV-cache buffers can be exported to and imported from other ranks.

k.s: Opens a cudaIpcMemHandle with lazy peer access and wraps the pointer as a byte tensor whose deleter closes the handle; returns nullopt when the open fails.
Produces a cudaIpcMemHandle plus byte count for a device pointer and returns it as opaque py::bytes.
Allocates page-rounded device memory with cuMemAlloc and wraps it as a 1-D byte tensor freed via cuMemFree, deliberately bypassing torch's caching allocator so the block is IPC-exportable.
Registers alloc_tensor / export_ipc_tensor / import_ipc_tensor into the cuda_utils pybind submodule.

nodes.s: Shared header for the device-memory utilities: declares the alloc/IPC API implemented by either cuda_utils.cpp or asc_utils.cpp, and supplies the WITH_NPU-switched get_default_device() and make_from_blob() helpers used throughout the C++ engine.

k.s: Returns the engine's device type for this build — kPrivateUse1 under WITH_NPU, kCUDA otherwise; pulled into the global namespace so every csrc call site stays platform-agnostic.

nodes.s: KV-cache block allocator for the C++ scheduler: an intrusive doubly-linked free list with ref-counted pinning, wrapped by a mutex-guarded BlockManager and an RAII guard that allocates a sequence's blocks and its state slot together.

k.s: Intrusive doubly-linked free list over block ids 1..n-1 (id 0 means empty), with ref-counted pin/free so a block shared by forked sequences is only returned once the last reference drops.
Thread-safe facade over Blocks: can_allocate/allocate/free/pin in both locked and _nolock flavours, so the scheduler can batch many operations under one acquisition.
RAII guard locking the block manager and the optional state manager together, and the only place a sequence gets its block table plus state slot allocated atomically.
Checks that both a block run and a state slot are available before allocating either, returning false for a retryable shortage and hard-failing on AllocStatus::NEVER.

nodes.s: Computes an FP8-equivalent FLOP estimate per scheduled request so the engine can report MFU: attention (including compressed-pair counts and SWA ranges), MLP / router / hidden-compression / Engram per-row costs, and the logits projection — draft (MTP) and padding work are excluded on purpose.

k.s: Precomputes per-row and per-pair FLOP coefficients from the model metadata once at construction, then answers calc_flops(q, k) cheaply for every request the scheduler lays out.
Returns (attention, total) FP8-equivalent FLOPs for one scheduled request from its q/k lengths, prompt flag and SWA valid start; total already includes attention.
Builds the per-layer attention cost model — core and index attention, dense vs sparse compression ratios, k-projection and the YoCo producer/consumer split — into reusable PairTerm coefficients.
Per-row FLOP cost of the Engram path (n-gram embedding projection and gating), split into producer and consumer layer contributions.

nodes.s: Implements BlockLoadPlanBuilder: turns per-sequence token ranges into the flat int32 [N,4] segment table (src_block_id, src_begin, src_end, dst_offset) that the KV-cache load kernels consume, merging adjacent segments and encoding zero-fill as src_block_id = -1.

k.s: Walks a sequence's block table over [token_begin, token_end) and emits one segment per touched page, clipping the first and last page to the requested token bounds.
Emits segments for a ring-buffer (sliding-window) source block, splitting into two segments when the requested range wraps past the end of the block.
Materializes the accumulated segments into a pinned int32 [N,4] tensor plus total_k, the finished BlockLoadPlan handed to the load kernel.

nodes.s: Declares the block-load plan types: BlockLoadSegment / BlockLoadPlan (an int32 [N,4] segment tensor plus total_k) and the BlockLoadPlanBuilder that assembles them for paged and ring (SWA) KV layouts.

k.s: The finished plan handed to the KV-cache load kernel: a segment tensor and the total token count it produces, zero-filled segments included.
Accumulates zero-fill, paged and ring-buffer ranges against a fixed source block size and builds the segment tensor once.

nodes.s: Contract for the host-side input-metadata builders: the PrepareArgs parameter pack (block and SWA sizes, Engram n-gram settings, CP size, YoCo truncation mode, compression ratios) plus the prepare_prompt / prepare_decode entry points for the base and V4 layouts.

k.s: One parameter pack shared by every prepare_prompt_* / prepare_decode_* builder, with prompt-only, decode-only and V4-only fields grouped and commented; `out` carries pre-allocated tensors for graph replay.

nodes.s: Model-agnostic half of per-step input construction: fills pinned CPU tensors for input ids, positions, seqlens, Engram n-gram rows and the decode block tables / context lens, reusing caller-supplied `out` buffers when graph replay needs stable addresses.

k.s: Writes one Engram n-gram row by walking back max_ngram_size compressed tokens from `pos`, padding out of range positions and truncating the row once an image sentinel is crossed.
Builds the paged KV load plan for a whole batch at a given compression ratio, emitting a single zero-fill segment for sequences with no cached tokens.
Core of the host-side batch layout: fills input ids, positions, cumulative seqlens and the Engram n-gram block that both prompt and decode steps share.
Prompt-step wrapper over prepare_common_base, adding the prefill-specific seqlen_k and query-index tensors.
Decode-step wrapper over prepare_common_base, adding context lengths, the padded block table and the per-sequence query indices.

nodes.s: DeepSeek-V4-specific input-metadata builder layered on the base one: multi-ratio compressed block tables, SWA ring-buffer load plans, and the YoCo consumer-prefill truncation metadata (per-row visibility windows, CP mirror and pad scalars) for both prompt and decode steps.

k.s: Fills the tensors prompt and decode V4 steps share — compressed block tables per ratio, SWA state ids, pivots and the sparse/dense index metadata — in either allocate or fill-in-place mode.

Computes one query row's visible key interval under YoCo truncation as the max of the sliding-window bound, the rectangle bound and the zero-state valid start, split into the carried-state and in-chunk parts.
Builds the full YoCo consumer-prefill truncation metadata: per-row visibility offsets and lengths, clip prefixes, compaction indices and the CP mirror/pad scalars.
Builds the sliding-window load plan from each sequence's ring-buffer state block, clamping the window to swa_valid_start so recomputed zero states are never read.
Full prompt-step metadata for V4: delegates to prepare_prompt_base, adds the V4 common tensors, the SWA and per-ratio paged load plans, and the YoCo truncation block.
Full decode-step metadata for V4: base decode tensors plus the V4 common block, compressed block tables and the SWA ring metadata the decode kernels need.

nodes.s: Variable-length MTP (speculative decoding) batch planner: tracks median sampler and forward-step runtimes, then picks the throughput-optimal total query count against a measured (batch_size, forward_ms) curve and hands each request its seqlen_q by sorting draft tokens on predicted accept rate.

k.s: Nine-sample sliding median of sampler step time, reported only once at least five samples exist.
Fits a per-token slope on top of the static forward-time curve: aggregates recent residuals by graph size, takes a median per graph, then a median of those medians so each graph size weighs equally.
Owns the decode performance curve and the runtime estimators, and turns a scheduled batch into per-request seqlen_q values that maximize expected accepted tokens per millisecond.

Picks the best total query count by walking draft tokens in descending accept-rate order against the forward+sampler time model, then distributes the extra query slots back to the requests that earned them.

nodes.s: Turns a finished step into per-request outputs: a flat RequestOutput POD, a 10k-slot placement-new pool handed to Python as raw uint64 pointers to avoid per-token object churn, and build_request_outputs() which de-interleaves sampled and MTP-accepted tokens, logprobs and top-k into one output per token.

k.s: Flat per-token result record — token id, logprobs, top-k, finish reason, prompt logprobs and the MTP draft/accept counters — sized so a whole step's outputs live contiguously in the pool.
Fixed 10,000-slot arena of RequestOutput built with aligned_alloc and placement new; Python returns consumed pointers through release() and the pool hard-fails if it is ever exhausted.

Walks the scheduler's finished batch and the sampler's tensors to emit one RequestOutput per generated token, splitting the accepted-token columns of a speculative step and attaching prompt logprobs and confidence scores.

nodes.s: Assembles the sampler's input tensors for one step — temperature / top-p / top-k rows, per-sequence seeds, selected token indices, EOS-suppression rows, prompt-logprob slices and the MTP info read/write slots — then ships them to the device with non-blocking copies out of pinned memory.

k.s: Single pass over the batch that sizes every sampler tensor, fills the pinned host buffers and returns the layered SamplerInputs; the driver group is skipped entirely on context-parallel follower ranks.

nodes.s: Declares the layered sampler-input structs (logits transform, sampling kernel, prompt-logprob, prefill, speculative, decode and driver groups) that prepare_sampler_inputs() fills, plus its signature.

k.s: The work only the context-parallel driver rank does: the sampling kernel tensors, top-logprob width, golden-token reference and the optional prefill and speculative sub-groups.
Top-level sampler input bundle — selected token and prompt indices plus the optional decode and driver groups; `driver` being absent is how a CP follower is signalled.

nodes.s: Accumulates prompt logprobs across chunked-prefill steps into each SequenceMetadata, returning the full list only on the last prompt chunk and an empty list for requests that never asked for them.

k.s: Appends this chunk's prompt logprobs to the per-sequence accumulator and emits the completed vector only once the final prompt chunk has run, distinguishing 'not requested' (nullopt) from 'not ready' (empty).

nodes.s: Entry point of the `engine` pybind submodule: calls the three per-translation-unit registrars for the sequence, scheduler and output bindings.

k.s: Registers the sequence, scheduler and output bindings into the engine submodule, in that order.

nodes.s: Declares the engine submodule initializer and its three sub-registrars (sequence / scheduler / output), each kept in its own translation unit to contain pybind11 template instantiation cost.

pybind11 bindings for the output path: RequestOutput (every field also exposed as a static get_<field>(ptr) accessor for the raw-pointer fast path), RequestOutputPool, build_request_outputs and prepare_sampler_inputs together with the sampler-input structs.

k.s: Registers the output and sampler-input classes and the two free functions, generating the paired def_readonly / static pointer accessor for each RequestOutput field via a macro.

nodes.s: pybind11 bindings for the scheduling path: BlockManager, FlopsEstimator, SchedulerOutputs (with zero-copy numpy views over the scheduler's clone/zero state buffers) and the Scheduler itself, plus update_prompt_logprobs.

k.s: Registers the scheduler-side classes and exposes SchedulerOutputs' state-clone buffers as borrowed zero-copy numpy arrays valid only until the next schedule() call.

nodes.s: pybind11 bindings for Sequence / SequenceData / SequenceMetadata and the ZOS helpers: flattens Python's keyword arguments into the C++ SequenceInit struct once at the boundary and exposes a vectorized compressed-token encoder for the Engram tokenizer.

k.s: Packs Python's flat constructor arguments into the grouped SequenceInit struct, defaulting a request to schedulable only when it carries no multimodal data.
Registers Sequence, SequenceData and SequenceMetadata with property helpers that expose nested C++ sub-state as flat Python attributes, plus the ZOS entry points.

nodes.s: The continuous-batching scheduler, written entirely in C++: keeps the waiting / running / prompted queues, votes across the data-parallel group on whether a step is prefill or decode, chunks prompts without splitting an image, allocates blocks and MTP info slots, preempts under KV pressure, and folds sampler results back into sequence state.

k.s: One step's scheduling decision: the chosen sequences, prompt-vs-decode flag, token counts, per-request seqlen_q, FLOP estimates, and borrowed references to the state clone/zero buffers.

Owns the request queues, block and state managers, MTP slot pool, FLOP estimator and MTPVarlen planner, and implements the whole admit / chunk / preempt / retire lifecycle for the three engine types (NORMAL, PROMPT, COMPLETION).

Decides the step type for a NORMAL engine: at ALL points every rank must have prefill work, at ANY points one suffices, and a second allreduce falls back to decode when nobody actually managed to schedule a prompt — the guard against a prefill/decode livelock.

Builds a prompt step from the waiting queue: enforces prompt limits and the prefill seqlen_k budget, chunks long prompts on image-safe boundaries, allocates blocks plus state, and stops at the first unschedulable head of queue.
Builds a decode step from the running queue: appends slots, preempts victims when blocks run out, and delegates to MTPVarlen to pick each request's speculative query length.
Public per-step entry point: runs _schedule, then fills in seqlen statistics and the attention / total TFLOP estimates used for MFU reporting.

Folds a completed step back into sequence state — appends sampled and accepted tokens, updates MTP bookkeeping and structured-output matchers, applies stop conditions and moves finished sequences out of the running queue.
Frees a victim sequence's blocks under KV pressure, either aborting it outright or resetting it for recompute and pushing it back to the head of the waiting queue.
Clones a running sequence into a new branch, duplicating the block table with pinning and cloning the state slot so the two branches diverge without copying the KV cache.
Shifts each sequence's MTP accept-rate history by one step and records the new draft tokens and confidences, keeping schedule_cnt and process_cnt in the pairing MTPVarlen::schedule relies on.
Applies the step's pending state-clone and zero-state requests to the recurrent state blocks, the companion of SchedulerOutputs' clone_states / zero_states buffers.

nodes.s: Core request state for the C++ engine: token storage, the sampling and stopping snapshots captured once from Python SamplingParams, KV-cache and schedule sub-states, MTP draft/accept bookkeeping, and the per-step SequenceMetadata view recycled through an object pool.

k.s: Maps a terminal SequenceStatus to the user-visible finish reason string, including the preemption case surfaced as insufficient_system_resource.
Token-id storage for one sequence with the prompt length recorded, constructible directly from a numpy int32 array to avoid a per-token Python conversion.
Plain-old-data snapshot of the sampling parameters, captured once from the Python SamplingParams object so the hot path never touches Python attributes.

Per-sequence speculative-decoding state: golden tokens, draft and accepted tokens, two generations of accept rates and confidences, the MTP info slot and the schedule/process counters that say which round each rate belongs to.
The sequence's cache view: block table, state slot, prefix-hit count, SWA valid start and an optimistic token counter that is advanced before a step and committed after it.
Queue-side state: status, schedulability, branch id, chunked-prefill remainder and checkpoints, plus the in-flight token accounting that async scheduling depends on.
A whole request: request identity, token input, generation parameters, cache, MTP, structured-output and schedule sub-states, with the block-count and recompute-reset logic the scheduler calls.

The per-step view a Sequence presents to the model runner and sampler — reference members into the owning Sequence (or a self-owned block for Python-built dummies) — allocated from an object pool and refreshed in place each step.

nodes.s: Small engine-wide helpers: the SPRINT_VARS macro that formats variable names and values into TORCH_CHECK messages, and get_nextn_from_env() which reads DEEPINFER_USE_NEXTN_DECODE.

k.s: Reads the DEEPINFER_USE_NEXTN_DECODE environment variable (default 5) so the C++ scheduler's speculative depth matches the Python-side default in deepinfer/environ.py.

nodes.s: Host-side preparation for ZOS (zero-overhead scheduling) decode steps: remaps this step's sequences onto the previous step's slot order so GPU-resident state can be reused, builds the padded seqlen / block-table / token tensors including Engram n-gram rows, and patches sampling metadata after the GPU corrects seqlen_q.

k.s: Fills the padded input-id, fresh-token, Engram n-gram and sliding-window token tensors for a ZOS decode step, mapping raw ids through the compressed Engram vocabulary where one is configured.

Computes the remap from this step's sequences to their slots in the previous step — fast path when the order is unchanged, hash lookup otherwise — and returns nothing when the two steps share no requests.
Builds the full padded decode input bundle for a ZOS step: token tensors, per-sequence seqlens, compressed block tables and query indices, sized to the padded batch so graph replay stays valid.
Rewrites the step's SequenceMetadata after the GPU has resolved the real per-request seqlen_q, so the sampler and output builder see the accepted lengths rather than the optimistic scheduled ones.

nodes.s: Declares the three ZOS entry points — remap computation, padded decode-input construction and the post-forward sampling-metadata fixup — along with the wide tuple type the decode path returns to Python.

Platform-neutral handles for timing inside a captured device graph: EventHandle (record / query / elapsed_time with the capture-external flag), GraphHandle for enumerating a graph's event-record nodes, and EventRecordNodeHandle for swapping which event a node records into.

k.s: Wraps a captured platform graph and exposes its event-record nodes; equality and hashing are on the instantiated exec graph so Python can key caches by graph.
A device timing event that can be recorded onto a stream with the capture-external flag — the flag that turns a record inside a graph capture into an event-record graph node.
Handle to one event-record node of a captured graph, allowing the event it records into to be read and swapped so each replay can be timed with fresh events.

nodes.s: Ascend/NPU implementation of the graph-timer handles — every entry point throws 'NPU graph timer primitives are not implemented yet', so in-graph timing is currently a CUDA-only capability.

CUDA implementation of the graph-timer handles: creates events with cudaEventRecordWithFlags, walks a captured cudaGraph_t for cudaGraphNodeTypeEventRecord nodes, and rewrites a node's event in the instantiated exec graph so individual regions of a replay can be timed.

k.s: Enumerates the captured graph's nodes twice (count, then fetch) and keeps only the event-record ones, pairing each with the exec graph needed to patch it.

nodes.s: Registers the graph_timer pybind submodule, exposing EventHandle, EventRecordNodeHandle and GraphHandle (with __eq__ / __hash__) so the Python runtime can time individual nodes of a captured graph.

k.s: Binds the three graph-timer handle classes, releasing the GIL around the blocking synchronize() call.

nodes.s: Top-level torch extension module: creates the cuda_utils, engine and graph_timer submodules and delegates to each one's pymodule_init — the single native entry point the Python package imports.

k.s: Defines the extension module and wires up its three submodules in order: device-memory utilities, the scheduling engine, and the graph timer.

nodes.s: Base class giving the block managers a pthread error-check mutex with a 20-second clocklock deadline and a hard assert that the GIL is not held while locking — the convention that keeps the GIL-releasing scheduler from deadlocking against Python threads.

k.s: Protected lock_/unlock_ pair over a PTHREAD_ERRORCHECK mutex, inherited by BlockManager so locking discipline is enforced in one place.
Asserts the GIL is not held, tries the mutex uncontended first, then falls back to a monotonic clocklock with a 20-second deadline that hard-fails rather than hanging.

nodes.s: Header-only std::format logger for the C++ side: a DEEPINFER_CPP_LOG_LEVEL-driven level filter, microsecond timestamps, a mutex-guarded stdout writer, and the LOG_INFO / LOG_WARN / LOG_ERROR macros used across csrc.

k.s: Resolves the log level once from DEEPINFER_CPP_LOG_LEVEL into a function-local static, defaulting to INFO on an unset or unrecognized value.
Formats the current wall-clock time as MM-DD HH:MM:SS.microseconds for the log prefix.

nodes.s: Recycles pybind-owned C++ objects: the pool keeps released py::object shells and placement-news a new T into them, so hot per-step types such as SequenceMetadata cost no Python allocation per scheduling step.

k.s: Template pool over py::object shells: allocate() either casts a fresh T or destroys and placement-news into a recycled shell, and release() returns only instances flagged as pool-allocated.

nodes.s: Barrel for the hardware-neutral device discovery API, re-exporting the fourteen functions of device.py (accelerator_kind, visible/physical device queries, NUMA and TFLOPS helpers) as the single import surface used by the engine, examples and tests.

Huawei Ascend NPU discovery backend that enumerates devices purely from /dev/davinci* nodes and /sys/class/ubcore sysfs metadata, and resolves per-device NUMA affinity from `npu-smi info -t topo` cross-referenced with lscpu topology.

k.s: Enumerates /sys/class/ubcore udma entries sorted by index or by (controller, die, entity), giving a stable device ordering on Ascend.
Returns the sorted indices of /dev/davinci<N> device nodes, the primary signal that Ascend NPUs are present.
Reports whether this host has Ascend NPUs, by checking /dev/davinci_manager, davinci device nodes, or a ubcore entry with a non-zero ub_totalues count.
Walks the ubcore entries and returns one tuple per NPU with its identifiers and raw NUMA metadata read from sysfs.
Builds a device-index to NUMA-node map by parsing `npu-smi info -t topo` CPU affinity lists and picking the NUMA node whose physical cores overlap each NPU's affinity mask the most.
Resolves an Ascend device's NUMA node, preferring the npu-smi topology map and falling back to sysfs metadata with the die-pairing correction ((raw//2)*2 + index%2).

nodes.s: Parses `lscpu -p` output into a NUMA-node to physical-CPU-core mapping, keeping only the lowest logical CPU per (node, socket, core) so hyperthread siblings are collapsed. Shared by the Ascend NUMA lookup and CPU affinity binding.

k.s: Runs `lscpu -p=CPU,NODE,SOCKET,CORE,ONLINE` and returns online physical core ids grouped by NUMA node, one id per core rather than per hardware thread.

nodes.s: The hardware-neutral device layer: detects whether the host is NVIDIA, Ascend or CPU-only and dispatches every device query (counts, visible-device env var, physical ids, NUMA node, BF16 TFLOPS ceiling, SM major version) to the matching backend. This is the platform-abstraction seam the rest of DeepInfer sees.

k.s: Detects the host accelerator once per process, returning 'ascend', 'nvidia' or 'cpu'; every other dispatch in the platform layer keys off this value.
Number of accelerators physically present on the host, dispatched to the Ascend or NVIDIA backend (0 on a CPU-only host).
Parses the backend's visible-devices environment variable into a tuple of device ids, falling back to all physical devices when it is unset.
Number of accelerators visible to this process after CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES / ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES filtering.
Maps a process-local rank to the physical device identifier it is bound to, honouring the visible-device mask.
Writes the backend-appropriate visible-devices environment variable, so callers never have to know whether the host wants CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES or ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES.
Computes and sets the slice of devices a given rank owns from devices_per_rank plus an offset, the per-process device partitioning used when launching data-parallel workers.
Backend-dispatched NUMA node of a physical device, used by the topology layer to pin a worker's CPUs and memory near its accelerator.
Physical accelerator count ignoring any visibility mask; used by test harnesses and launch scripts that need to partition the whole node.
Hard-coded peak BF16 TFLOPS for the detected accelerator (432 on Ascend, 2500/2250 on SM10.x depending on host arch), the denominator for the engine's roofline and FLOPs-budget math.
True when the host GPU is an SM100-class NVIDIA part, read via NVML without creating a CUDA context; gates the SM100-only fast paths such as deep_gemm bf16_gemm_nt.

nodes.s: NVIDIA discovery backend reading /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus, /dev/nvidia* and sysfs for device enumeration and NUMA node, plus a ctypes NVML binding that reads compute capability without ever creating a CUDA context.

k.s: Sorted indices of /dev/nvidia<N> device nodes, the fallback enumeration when /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus is unavailable.
Reads a GPU's NUMA node from its procfs/sysfs entry, raising rather than guessing when the metadata is missing.
Lazily loads libnvidia-ml through ctypes, initializes NVML and declares the argtypes/restypes for the three entry points used; returns None when no driver or library is present.
Returns (major, minor) CUDA compute capability via NVML without creating a CUDA context, so it is safe to call before CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is finalized.

nodes.s: Barrel exposing the three NUMA/affinity helpers (bind_numa, set_cpu_affinity, which_numa) from bind.py.

NUMA lookup and process binding via a ctypes libnuma binding: resolves the NUMA node of a visible accelerator ordinal or an InfiniBand device, then pins the calling process's CPU affinity and memory policy (MPOL_BIND) to that node.

k.s: Loads libnuma.so.1 through ctypes and declares the signatures for numa_node_to_cpus, numa_sched_setaffinity, set_mempolicy and friends.

Returns the NUMA node for either a visible accelerator ordinal (resolved through physical_device_id and the backend's device_numa_node, with Ascend's trailing-digit id parsing) or an mlx5 InfiniBand device read from sysfs.
Pins the current process to one NUMA node: sets CPU affinity from the node's cpumask and applies MPOL_BIND so allocations stay local; returns -1 and prints errno on failure.

nodes.s: Pytest configuration for the TileLang kernel tests: binds each xdist worker to its own GPU at import time, points the tile_kernels benchmark/gpu-mem plugins at the local baseline directories, collects the non-test_*-named top-level kernel files, and skips tests whose kernel the selected backend has not implemented.

k.s: Binds a pytest-xdist worker to GPU (worker_id % num_gpus) by setting CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES (and the Ascend equivalent) before any CUDA-initializing import happens.

Collector hook that picks up top-level *.py files under tilelang_ops/ containing `def test_`, since the kernel reference tests are named after their op rather than matching pytest's test_*.py pattern.

Wrapper hook that converts the ops layer's KernelUnavailableError into a skip on Ascend (where the backend is incomplete) while keeping it fatal on NVIDIA, matching the exception by name to avoid importing the heavy ops module.

nodes.s: The DeepSeek-V4.1 vision encoder (deepseek_vit_opt): a 32-layer, 1024-dim ViT with RMSNorm, 2D rotary embeddings, varlen flash attention and SwiGLU MLP, with its architecture fixed by module constants rather than config. Execution-plane, DeepSeek-original code that delegates every dense op to an external kernel library.

k.s: bf16 matmul helper: bias goes through torch.addmm (cuBLAS), bias-free goes through deep_gemm.bf16_gemm_nt on SM100/Ascend with the output padded so the row stride is 16B-aligned, otherwise cublaslt_gemm_nt.
Patch embedding as a single flattened linear over [n, 3, p, p] patches, producing one embed_dim vector per patch.
Precomputes inverse-frequency rotary tables for the vision grid; the encoder builds cos/sin for a 4096-wide grid once at construction.
Non-causal varlen self-attention block: one fused QKV projection, in-place rotary via tile_kernels.apply_rotary, flash_attn.cute _flash_attn_fwd over cu_seqlens, then the output projection.
SwiGLU MLP with the hidden size rounded up to a multiple of 128; the gate activation is the fused tile_kernels swiglu_forward kernel.
One transformer block (pre-norm attention + pre-norm SwiGLU) that threads the residual through the norm kernel's fused add, materializing it explicitly only when return_added_residual is set.

Computes the contiguous device slice this engine rank owns from (engine_rank, cp_size, device_count) plus DEVICE_OFFSET, and writes CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES (and ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES on NPU).

Its print format is parsed by tests/models/test_offline_inference.py and must not change.

nodes.s: Build script for the deepinfer._C C++/CUDA extension: compiles the shared csrc/ sources (engine pybind layer, sequence/scheduler/output bindings, zero-overhead scheduling, input-metadata and sampling preparation, graph timer) as a CUDAExtension on NVIDIA or an NpuExtension on Ascend, selected by the deep_cluster accelerator probe.

Validates the native C++ FlopsEstimator against an independent NumPy reference that enumerates visible keys per query position, over all three YoCo truncation modes, prefill and decode, and boundary cases around SWA window, compression ratio, top-k and candidate-block edges.

k.s: The independent reference: enumerates one-based query positions, applies the YoCo cutoff and SWA valid-start masks, and accumulates logical GEMM FLOPs and visible-key counts layer by layer, including Engram, FP8 vs BF16 projections and both HC layouts.
Generates the (q, k, full_len, swa_valid_start) case grid: both sides of every SWA / compression-ratio / top-k / candidate-block boundary, two long-context extremes, and 128 seeded random points.
Parameterized over yoco_mode x prefill/decode, asserts the estimator matches the reference exactly on every generated case.
Forces BF16 projections and both HC layouts (shifted and not) even when the checkpoint is FP8, so those estimator branches are exercised.
Checks the mask-mode-only case where an Engram layer sits in the consumer half of the model, which compact mode forbids.

nodes.s: Harness that runs a multi-rank model regression in a spawned, session-isolated subprocess with a hard timeout, then SIGKILLs the whole process group so no data-parallel worker survives a partial failure.

k.s: Spawns the data-parallel entry point in its own session, asserts it finished inside the timeout with exit code 0, and unconditionally kills the process group afterwards.

nodes.s: Batch-invariance regression: with DEEPINFER_BATCH_INVARIANT=1, generating a prompt inside a 64-sequence batch and generating it alone must produce identical token ids, logprobs and top-k logprobs on every data-parallel rank.

Pytest entry that runs the batch-invariance body across all DP ranks for each parameterized case.

nodes.s: Numerical-consistency regression on freshly generated image+text prompts: compares the logprobs produced step by step during decode against the logprobs of a single full prefill over the same tokens, requiring prompt logprobs to match exactly and the decode KL divergence to stay under the case's bound.

k.s: Builds the VL prompt set (3 prompts of 16k expanded tokens) with seeded random images, matching benchmark.py's image prompt mode.

One rank's body: generates with the VL prompts, re-runs the full prompt+output sequence as a single prefill, asserts the prompt logprobs are bit-identical and accumulates the cosine/RMSE/Chebyshev/KL diffs of the decode logprobs.
Pytest entry that validates the EP/CP divisibility and the max_kl vs forced-top-k precondition, then runs the KL body across DP ranks.

nodes.s: The end-to-end offline-inference golden regression: runs examples/offline_inference.py as a subprocess under the platform's pinned parallel configuration (EP16/CP8 on Ascend, EP4/CP2 on NVIDIA), parses the decode perplexities out of its stdout and compares them exactly against offline_decode_ppl.json for the DP ranks this node owns.

k.s: Reads the per-rank golden for this platform and workload and validates it covers a contiguous DP rank range with finite, positive values.
Extracts the `DP <rank>; ... decode_ppl=<value>` lines from the script's stdout into a per-rank list of perplexities.
Runs the inference script with a timeout, streaming and capturing both stdout and stderr, and kills the whole process group on timeout or failure.

Builds the environment (device offset, master port, NextN depth, batch-invariant mode on NVIDIA), runs examples/offline_inference.py with the pinned EP/CP, and validates the parsed PPLs cover exactly this node's DP ranks with the expected sample counts.
Loads the golden, asserts its rank set matches the current parallel configuration, collects fresh PPLs and compares them sample by sample for exact equality.
CI entry running the short workload with structured-output validation enabled.

nodes.s: Long-context variant of the offline-inference golden regression (16k in / 4k out), split out of the short CI workload behind the long_context marker.

k.s: Runs the shared offline-inference golden comparison with long_context enabled.

nodes.s: Statistical correctness test for the sampler: generates 128 rollouts per sampling configuration (greedy and three temperature/top-p settings), turns each sampled token into a randomized PIT quantile from sum_smaller_probs and token_logprobs, and KS-tests those quantiles against U(0,1), failing when the p-value collapses.

k.s: Survival function of the Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic, computed from the series expansion so no SciPy dependency is needed.
One-sample KS test of a value set against U(0,1), returning the statistic and its p-value.

Randomized probability-integral transform: maps each sampled token to a uniform quantile using the cumulative mass below it and its own probability, with a seeded jitter inside the token's probability interval.

One rank's body: runs the rollouts for each sampling configuration, collects PIT quantiles separately for all accepted tokens and for the first (non-speculative) token per step, KS-tests both and records an error when a p-value falls below 1e-5.
Nightly pytest entry running the sampler correctness body across DP ranks with a two-hour timeout.

nodes.s: Batch-invariance regression for the inline vision encoder (ViT + downsample + aligner) with no LLM: for nine image sizes, every image's embeds must be bit-identical (torch.equal) to its single-image baseline, both when a batch repeats one shape and when a batch mixes shapes at random.

k.s: One rank's body: loads the VE-only model, builds the per-shape baselines, then runs the single-shape repeat batches and the seeded mixed-shape batches, collecting every embed that differs from its baseline.
Pytest entry running the VE batch-invariance body across 8 DP ranks.

nodes.s: The cache-engine test suite: exercises GPUCacheInterface.select_state_slice_to_store and load_state_from_store_to_prefill_cache under the three DEEPINFER_PREFILL_STORE_EXTRA_STATE configurations, and separately validates the KV-cache layout math (C1/C2 compression ratios, KVCacheManager.finalize drift assertion, offset monotonicity and alignment) plus the YoCo SWA dump/restore path.

k.s: Deep-copies the model config while breaking the inter-layer aliasing of attn_module_list, so per-layer rewrites in one test cannot overwrite each other through a shared AttrDict.
Base suite holding the shared env setup (backtracking tokens, YoCo mask mode and keep-tokens) and the randomly filled state-cache fixture whose shape comes from GPUCacheInterface._kvcache_layout.
The DEEPINFER_PREFILL_STORE_EXTRA_STATE=True suite: checks the state slice selected for the store and the restore back into the prefill cache, including the extra-state region.
The same store/restore checks with extra state disabled, where the initialization path and the stored layout differ.
Edge-case suite with extra state enabled but DEEPINFER_PREFILL_STORE_EXTRA_SIZE=0, where the extra region degenerates to empty.

Layout-level suite over the retained C1/C2 compression ratios: ModelMetadata must accept them, KVCacheManager.finalize's drift assertion must hold, and the computed offsets must be monotonic, non-overlapping and aligned. Pure config math with no KV buffer allo
Sizes the state buffer with a throwaway KVCacheManager, allocates random state, then re-runs the manager over every runtime attention module to produce the per-layer KVCache views.
Verifies that YoCo compact prefill and consumer-side-off produce the same layout, and that the disk dump keeps only the stored SWA region while in-GPU transfers carry all of the state.
Asserts ModelMetadata rejects configs that still request the removed C4/C128 compression ratios, compress_overlap or APE, with an error naming the feature.

nodes.s: Torch-free package root: appends the platform-tagged `_so/<accelerator>-<arch>` directory to `__path__` so NVIDIA and Ascend builds coexist in one source tree, presets CUDA/NVML/symmetric-memory env vars, and exposes `PLATFORM` through a lazy module `__getattr__`.

k.s: Computes the `<accelerator>-<arch>` tag (e.g. `nvidia-x86_64`) naming the built extension directory, using only env vars and `deep_cluster.hardware` so no torch import or device init leaks into the package root.

nodes.s: Defines `AttrDict`, the attribute-access mapping every model config in the project is expressed in, normalizing nested dicts on write, plus a recursive `merge` used to overlay config fragments.

k.s: Recursively merges two mappings into a new dict, letting nested config fragments be overlaid without mutating either side.

Dict subclass with attribute access that wraps nested mappings into `AttrDict` on every write, and overloads `+` / `|` to produce merged copies — the container every `model_cfg` in the project is built from.

nodes.s: vLLM-derived configuration objects (`ModelConfig`, `CacheConfig`, `ParallelConfig`, `SchedulerConfig`) the engine is constructed from; DeepSeek dropped vLLM's tensor-parallel fields in favour of data / context / expert / engram parallel sizes and loads `model_cfg` straight from the HF directory.

KV-cache configuration — block size, GPU memory utilization and lookahead tokens up front; block counts, per-block bytes and per-sequence state bytes are filled in after the worker memory-profiling pass.

Distributed-execution configuration. Notably there is no tensor-parallel field: the axes are data, context, expert and engram parallel size, plus the engine rank / group rank and the engine's `EngineType` role.

Scheduler limits handed to the C++ scheduler: max batched tokens and sequences, max model length and its runtime upper bound, chunked prefill, preempted-request policy and the prefill attempt intervals.
Derives the default `max_num_batched_tokens` from the model length and max concurrent sequences when the caller leaves it unset.

k.s: Single-writer / multi-reader ring buffer in POSIX shared memory with per-chunk reader flags; picklable via a `Handle` so worker processes can attach to the driver's segment.

The broadcast channel itself: local readers get the shared-memory ring plus a ZeroMQ XPUB socket for oversized chunks, remote readers get a TCP PUB socket; handles subscriber handshakes, busy-wait acquire of read/write slots and `broadcast_object` over a proce

nodes.s: vLLM-derived `EngineArgs` dataclass: seeds the zero-overhead-scheduling and multimodal-pool env vars from the chosen `EngineType`, then expands into the four engine configs. DeepSeek's variant carries data/context/expert/engram parallel sizes instead of tensor parallelism.

k.s: User-facing engine argument dataclass. `__post_init__` seeds `DEEPINFER_ZERO_OVERHEAD_SCHEDULING` and `DEEPINFER_USE_MULTIMODAL_POOL` from the `EngineType` and rearms them, and `create_engine_configs` expands the flat args into the four config objects.

nodes.s: Declares the `EngineType` enum (NORMAL / PROMPT / COMPLETION) that picks the engine's prefill-decode disaggregation role — kept in sync with `csrc/engine/scheduler.hpp` — and whether zero-overhead scheduling defaults on.

k.s: Enum of engine roles — NORMAL (prompts and completions), PROMPT (prefill only) and COMPLETION (decode only) — mirroring the C++ `EngineType`; also decides whether zero-overhead scheduling is on by default.

k.s: Holds a step's sequence metadata, pooled request outputs and clone/zero block unpins until the next `pre_sampler_sync`, so the caller is guaranteed to have read them and the recycling overlaps GPU compute.

nodes.s: DeepSeek-original per-engine profiling endpoint: `POST /profile` captures N torch-profiler steps on the driver GPU only and blocks until the trace is on disk, served from an asyncio loop on a daemon thread and gated by `DEEPINFER_PROFILE_HTTP_ENABLE`.

k.s: Runs the profiling HTTP server on a daemon-thread asyncio loop and advances the torch profiler from the engine's step loop; a request awaits a Future while the loop stays responsive, so a second concurrent request gets an immediate 409.

nodes.s: DeepSeek-original engine telemetry: sliding windows over per-step stats yield throughput, MFU, TTFT, MTP acceptance rate, MoE load-balance ratio and KV/state cache usage, emitted from a background logging thread so the step loop never blocks on I/O.

k.s: Background thread that drains the log queue, staggering the first emit by rank so eight ranks on a node do not interleave their stats lines.

Per-step record the engine hands the logger: batch shape, sequence-length sums, attention and total TFLOPs, first-token latencies, cached/generated/verified token counts, batch confidence error and MoE load-balance ratio.
The fully reduced view of one logging interval — throughputs, MFU, MTP acceptance rates, cache usages, queue depths and TTFT percentiles — that the log lines are rendered from.
Small deque-backed sliding window of timestamped payloads with `trim` and `sum`, the primitive every throughput and load-balance statistic is accumulated in.

Owns the sliding windows, CUDA/CPU timer merging and logging cadence; reads scheduler and state-manager counters off its engine back-reference, computes throughput/MFU/TTFT/MoE aggregates and queues the rendered lines to the logging thread.

nodes.s: vLLM-derived `LLM` convenience wrapper for offline batched inference: builds `EngineArgs`, feeds prompts into `LLMEngine` and drives `step()` to completion behind a tqdm bar. This release ships no online-serving entrypoint.

k.s: Offline batched-inference facade: constructs `EngineArgs` and `LLMEngine`, adds prompts with their sampling params, and `_run_engine` loops `step()` until every request finishes, cloning pooled outputs out before they are recycled.

nodes.s: Central registry of every `DEEPINFER_*` environment variable as a typed, cached `EnvVar` descriptor on the `envs` class, with `rearm()` / `rearm_all()` to re-read a variable after startup code mutates it.

k.s: Descriptor that parses one environment variable on first access and caches the result on the owner, with `int`/`float`/`bool`/`str`/`choice` constructors for the common types.
The single declaration site for every `DEEPINFER_*` knob, grouped by subsystem — platform, runtime, distributed comms, MoE/expert parallelism, attention, MTP, profiling and debugging.
Re-evaluates every cached EnvVar descriptor. The test suite's autouse fixture calls it after restoring os.environ so env-driven feature flags do not leak between tests.

nodes.s: Lazy barrel for the HF integration package: callers outside the package import `load_hf_model_config`, `get_hf_tokenizer` and the checkpoint-loading helpers from here, resolved on first access through module `__getattr__`.

Translates a DeepSeek-V4.1 HF `config.json` into the runtime `model_cfg`: per-layer attention module list, sliding-window and KV-compression specs, DFlash settings, MoE layout, the Engram table (sized from the sibling `tokenizer.json`) and the vision tower — rejecting architectures and quantization layouts the runtime does not support.

k.s: Builds the layer-sharing maps — each layer's index, KV and index-K source layer, plus the candidate-source block-scoring config — from the checkpoint's source-layer id lists.

Emits the attention spec for a KV-compressed layer: compression ratio and rope theta, the sparse index-attention head geometry (`index_topk`, k-proj/k-norm, rope dims), shared layer maps and the YaRN rope parameters when the checkpoint scales rope.

Assembles the per-layer attention spec list — sliding-window spec where `compress_ratio == 0`, compressed spec otherwise, a `None` placeholder for the lm head, then one DFlash spec per nextn MTP layer.
Extracts the MoE layout from the HF text config: intermediate size, routed and shared expert counts, experts per token, routing scoring function and top-k normalization.
Builds the DFlash (MTP draft model) config — sliding window, DSpark block size, target layer ids, Markov rank, noise token — including its own smaller MoE override.

Builds the Engram config when the checkpoint declares `engram_layer_ids`: one n-gram table per size from 2..max, their vocab/head/embedding dims, FP8 flags taken from the quantization config, and the path to the sibling `tokenizer.json` the compressed vocabula
Produces the vision-tower and MLP-projector configs (downsample-MLP-GELU projector sized from the vision hidden size and downsample ratio), which are also attached isomorphically under `vl_aligner`.

Entry point of the HF config parser: validates that the checkpoint declares exactly one architecture and that `ModelRegistry` supports it, then composes the attention module list, MoE, DFlash, Engram and vision sections into the `model_cfg` AttrDict the engine

nodes.s: Loads a checkpoint's HF tokenizer — resolving the class from `auto_map`, native `AutoTokenizer` or `LlamaTokenizerFast` — then pins BOS/PAD behaviour and registers the multimodal span tokens at the IDs the runtime hard-codes.

k.s: Applies the release checkpoint's token policy to a freshly loaded tokenizer: pins BOS/PAD behaviour and registers the multimodal span tokens at the exact IDs the runtime assumes.

Resolves and instantiates the tokenizer class for a checkpoint — bundled implementation via `auto_map`, native `AutoTokenizer`, or `LlamaTokenizerFast` — then runs the release fixups before returning it.

nodes.s: Eight-line helper that imports a Python file by filesystem path and returns a named class from it, used to pick up a checkpoint's bundled tokenizer implementation.

k.s: Imports a Python module from an explicit file path via `importlib.util` and returns the named class from it.

nodes.s: vLLM-derived logging setup (itself adapted from SkyPilot): `NewLineFormatter` prefixes every line of a multi-line record, `init_logger` hands out configured loggers, and DeepSeek adds a crash-header excepthook plus spawn/fork process subclasses that print rank context ahead of a traceback.

k.s: Log formatter that repeats the header prefix on every line of a multi-line record, so stack traces and multi-line stats blocks stay attributable to their rank.
Configures the root `deepinfer` logger once — stdout handler, `NewLineFormatter`, level from the environment — before any child logger is handed out.
Returns a module-scoped child of the configured `deepinfer` logger; the standard one-liner at the top of nearly every module in the project.

Installs `sys.excepthook` and optionally `threading.excepthook` so any uncaught exception prints the rank/crash header first, and a dying thread can take the process down instead of hanging the collective.
Mixin whose `run` installs the crash-header excepthook inside the child process, used by the spawn and fork `Process` subclasses the engine launches workers with.

nodes.s: Thin loader that parses `<model-dir>/config.json` through the HF parser and asserts the result is a multimodal V4.1 config carrying `vl_aligner`; deliberately import-light so `config.py` never drags in model implementations.

k.s: Loads `<model-dir>/config.json` through the HF parser and asserts the result is a multimodal V4.1 config carrying `vl_aligner`; the import of the HF package is deferred into the function body to keep the module torch-free.

nodes.s: Expert-parallel load balancer: accumulates per-expert token counts each step, periodically recomputes the physical-to-logical expert placement and shuffles expert weights in place, publishing the live maps that MoE dispatch, routing and the sampler read. `ExpertLoadBalancerManager` exposes the per-layer view and the process-global instance.

k.s: Rounds the requested number of redundant experts up until `num_routed_experts + extra` divides evenly across the EP group, so every rank holds the same number of physical experts.
Produces the day-zero physical-to-logical expert map: the routed experts in order, followed by the redundant slots replicating the first experts.

Per-EP-group load-balancer state: keeps a window of per-expert token counts, all-gathers them to derive the MoE load-balance ratio, and every `DEEPINFER_EXPERT_REARRANGEMENT_STEP_INTERVAL` steps recomputes the placement and shuffles weights — using symmetric-m
Maps each global MoE layer to the balancer and local layer index that owns it, fans `step()` out to every balancer, and aggregates their pending load-balance ratios for the stats logger.

Returns the currently active EPLB (expert-parallel load balancing) placement — the physical-to-logical expert map in force for this step. Read by the MoE layer to route tokens to locally resident experts.

nodes.s: The EPLB placement policy: a batched greedy assignment that spreads each logical expert's measured token load across its physical replicas, wrapped by `rebalance_experts_global`, which recomputes the whole physical expert map from the accumulated token histogram.

k.s: Batched greedy bin-packing over all MoE layers at once: repeatedly assigns the heaviest remaining logical expert to the least-loaded physical slot, respecting per-slot capacity.
Recomputes the global physical expert placement from the accumulated per-expert token histogram, returning the new physical-to-logical map, logical-to-physical map and replica counts for every layer.

nodes.s: Moves MoE expert weights between ranks when EPLB changes placement: a general NCCL batched-P2P path and a single-node path that reads peer weights directly through symmetric-memory / IPC mirrors, both rewriting the weight tensors in place.

k.s: Finds the expert slots whose new owner already holds that expert locally, so they can be satisfied by a local copy instead of a network transfer.
Builds the (sender rank, receiver rank) routes for one expert, pairing senders to receivers so the transfers spread evenly across the available source replicas.

General expert-weight shuffle: for every MoE layer, plans local copies and remote routes from the old and new physical maps and executes them with NCCL batched P2P, rewriting the weight tensors in place.
One layer of the P2P path: stages receives into scratch buffers, issues the batched isend/irecv set, then copies the arrived weights into their destination slots.

Single-node shuffle variant: publishes each layer's weights into the symmetric-memory mirror and lets every rank read its new experts directly out of peer IPC buffers, skipping the P2P exchange entirely.
One layer of the intra-node path: refreshes the symmetric-memory mirror, barriers the EP group, then pulls each needed expert from the owning rank's IPC buffer.

nodes.s: `MTPInfoPool` — GPU-resident storage for multi-token-prediction proposals indexed by scheduler slot (slot 0 reserved as padding), written by the `store_mtp_info` TileLang kernel; also supplies the placeholder draft token IDs the engine uses before a slot has produced proposals.

k.s: Returns the placeholder draft token IDs (vocab_size - 1, repeated nextn times) that match the contents of reserved pool slot 0.

GPU buffer module holding MTP draft tokens, logprobs (full-vocab or forced top-k), optional confidence and top-k indices, laid out as `(max_num_seqs + 1) * nextn` rows indexed by scheduler slot; `store` writes a batch of proposals through the `store_mtp_info`

nodes.s: vLLM-derived model loading: resolves the architecture through `ModelRegistry`, pads MoE redundant experts so they divide evenly across the EP group, finalizes parallel/runtime fields on `model_cfg`, builds the module on the meta device and loads the HF checkpoint — all under a watchdog that aborts the process if loading stalls.

k.s: Looks the checkpoint's architecture string up in `ModelRegistry` and raises with the supported list if it is unknown.
Context manager that starts a daemon timer and calls `os.abort()` if checkpoint loading has not finished within the timeout, turning a silent hang into a crash the launcher can see.

Builds the model class on the CUDA device under the config's default dtype, then asserts every parameter (and its FP8 scale factor) actually landed on the GPU before returning it in eval / no-grad mode.

Resolves `n_redundant_experts` for the backbone MoE and the DFlash MoE override before construction, rounding up so the physical expert count divides by the EP size and warning when the requested value had to move.
Writes the parallel and runtime fields the model builder needs onto an already-loaded `model_cfg` and initializes the construction environment.
Streams the HF safetensors shards into an already-built model and reports which checkpoint tensors were consumed, so missing or unexpected weights surface immediately.

nodes.s: vLLM-derived model registry reduced to a single entry: architecture `DeepseekV41ForCausalLM` maps to `DeepseekVLForCausalLM` in the `deepseek_vl` module, imported on demand.

k.s: Static architecture registry: `load_model_cls` imports the implementing module on demand and returns the class, `get_supported_archs` lists what the build supports (currently only `DeepseekV41ForCausalLM`).

nodes.s: Vision-language aligner: a small MLP built from `cfg` that projects vision-encoder features into the language model's hidden space; the vision forward pass calls `aligner.layers(x)` directly.

k.s: Builds the vision-to-language projection MLP from the aligner config; callers run `projector.layers(x)` directly rather than going through `forward`.

k.s: Gathers a tensor from every rank of a group and concatenates along `dim` on the destination rank, returning `None` elsewhere; short-circuits when the group has one member.

Broadcasts a mixed dict across the context-parallel group: non-tensor values and per-tensor `TensorMetadata` travel over the shared-memory object channel, the CUDA payloads then go over NCCL into receiver-allocated buffers.

Walks the meta model and converts every FP8-eligible weight to float8_e4m3fn with a matching scale-factor shape — per-row for Engram embeddings, square blocks elsewhere — skipping embeddings, heads and already-packed FP4 experts.

nodes.s: Cross-layer sharing of KV, indexer and index-K: a config-derived, fail-fast-validated topology (`SharedLayerTopology`), the per-forward slot container a source layer writes and later consumer layers read (`CrossLayerRuntime`), and a flattened per-layer view for consumers that only need the source flags.

k.s: Normalizes the sparse share-KV / share-index / share-index-K maps into full per-layer maps, checks that all copies of the shared config are identical, that sharing segments nest correctly, that no share-KV segment crosses the YoCo boundary and that candidate-b

One-forward mutable carrier for the six kinds of cross-layer values — shared hidden, pre-RoPE KV, top-k indices, candidate blocks, loaded prefill KV and loaded prefill index KV — plus the full-layout metadata and hidden the YoCo compaction boundary needs. A si
Flat per-runtime-layer view of the topology: the three source flags plus the candidate-block count and size.

nodes.s: Engram runtime — DeepSeek-V4.1's hash-indexed n-gram memory. Maps raw tokens onto a compressed vocabulary, fetches the rank-sharded n-gram embedding tables through DeepEP's `EngramBuffer`, projects them with the fused KV projection and gates the result into the hidden states with a fused TileKernels op.

k.s: Packs FP32-represented UE8M0 scale factors into the platform's scale dtype (4 per int32 on CUDA, 2 per int16 on Ascend) after asserting they are exact powers of two.

Process-wide singleton holding the raw-token-id to compressed-token-id lookup table on CPU and GPU; `encode` maps a token id array through the C++ single-pass encoder, sending out-of-vocabulary ids to the image sentinel.

This rank's shard of one layer's n-gram embedding table. Holds the weight until it is written into the DeepEP userbuffer, all-gathers the packed scale factors across the Engram parallel group, then releases its storage.

The per-layer Engram module: projects the fetched n-gram embeddings through the fused KV projection and gates them into the hidden states with `tile_kernels.engram.engram_gate_fwd`, using weights pre-fused at construction since they are constant during inferen

Owns the DeepEP `EngramBuffer` across all Engram layers: sizes and allocates it from the shard geometry, writes every layer's table (plus packed scale factors) once at startup, and per step turns a hash tensor into one lazy fetch hook per layer id.

nodes.s: Engram vocabulary compression and hash metadata: builds the normalized original-to-compressed token mapping on CPU, derives the static per-layer/per-head table layout from distinct primes, and materializes the hash multipliers, vocab sizes and offsets the Engram kernels consume.

k.s: Builds the original-token to compressed-token mapping by decoding each vocabulary entry and normalizing it (NFKC, accent strip, lowercase, whitespace collapse); invalid-UTF-8 pieces fall back to their raw spelling so distinct byte pieces cannot collide.

Frozen description of the n-gram table layout shared by parameter construction and runtime hashing; assigns each (layer, n-gram size, head) a distinct prime vocabulary size so hash ranges never overlap.
Materializes the per-layer hash tensors on device — odd random multipliers per n-gram size, the prime vocab sizes and the TileKernels-computed table offsets.

nodes.s: Engram parameter containers for the HF loader: the rank-local slice of the n-gram embedding table (row-padded to the LCM of 256 and the Engram parallel size) and the per-layer module holding the fused KV projection and the hidden/embed gate weights.

k.s: Allocates this rank's contiguous slice of one layer's n-gram table and tags the parameter with the metadata the loader and runtime need (layer id, per-head vocab sizes, row start, rows per part).

Per-layer HF-path container: the sharded n-gram table, the fused KV projection that expands the n-gram embedding to (hc_mult + 1) hidden vectors, and the hidden/embed gate weights. Forward lives in `engram.Engram`.

nodes.s: Mixin that adds the DFlash draft-attention metadata fields to InputMetadataV4 and builds them with one fused TileLang launch, so the fixed-stride draft layout can be captured and replayed inside a CUDA graph.

k.s: Holds the two DFlash-only tensors (draft-token SWA store slots and the per-draft-token KV index) and `build_dflash_input`, which copies the metadata and fills those fields from get_fused_dflash_get_input.

nodes.s: Defines the InputMetadata dataclass family (base, V4, VL, V4VL) carrying every per-step tensor the model forward consumes, plus flatten/broadcast serialization and the context-parallel mirror transform.

k.s: Base per-step input bundle (is_prompt, input_ids, positions, ngram_token_ids, masks) with the shared machinery: flatten to/from a dict for cross-rank broadcast, recursive tensor copy, and prepare_for_mirror_cp.

V4 metadata: SWA/compressed-attention slot mappings, compressor state block ids, cu_seqlens, load segments, block tables and the FlashMLA scheduling metadata; mixes in the YoCo and DFlash field groups.
Multi-modal extension carrying raw RGB bytes, per-image crop/patch counts and the image-token masks that the vision aligner turns into patches on GPU; image fields are prefill-only.
Diamond of InputMetadataVL and InputMetadataV4 that only overrides get_consumer_view, regathering images_seq_mask into the compacted layout the MoE image routing asserts on.

nodes.s: Builds the decode step's GPU input tensors on the ZOS (overlapped-scheduling) path: a C++ helper packs the per-sequence CPU state into pinned tensors, then TileLang gathers splice in the previous step's sampled and predicted tokens so the CPU never waits on the previous step's results.

k.s: NamedTuple of the pinned CPU tensors and derived scalars extracted once per decode step: cu_seqlens_q, block tables, state block ids, placeholder mask and the fresh/compressed token sources.
NamedTuple pairing DecodeInputsZOS with the reusable device buffers (positions, valid_token_mask, gate_force_random, context_lens, query_indices, block_tables) shared by every decode variant.
Calls the C++ prepare_decode_zos_inputs to batch all per-sequence CPU extraction into pinned tensors, then wraps them as DecodeInputsZOS.
Allocates (or reuses) one backing tensor and hands out contiguous slices for a group of same-shaped buffers, avoiding per-step allocation in the decode loop.
Allocates the device buffers shared across decode variants and returns them bundled as CommonDecodeBuffersZOS.

Fills input_ids and the Engram ngram_token_ids for the step by dispatching the gather_input_ids_zos and gather_engram_tokens_zos kernels, which read the previous step's sampled/predicted tokens via the remap table.
Post-step bookkeeping that writes the model outputs back into the ZOS buffers for the next step to consume.
Top-level V4 decode entry point: builds the common buffers, runs prepare_v4_decode_metadata on GPU and assembles the InputMetadataV4 the forward pass consumes.

nodes.s: Rotary position embedding layer and the YaRN long-context scaling variant, with a get_rope factory that caches instances by configuration; the actual rotation is delegated to the prebuilt TileKernels apply_rotary.

k.s: Base rotary embedding module: precomputes the cos/sin cache from inv_freq and applies it to q/k through the TileKernels apply_rotary op.
YaRN-scaled rotary embedding that interpolates low-frequency dimensions, extrapolates high-frequency ones via a linear ramp mask, and compensates attention entropy with an mscale factor.

Builds the clamped linear ramp used to blend interpolated and extrapolated inverse frequencies in YaRN.
Factory that parses the rope_scaling config and returns a cached RotaryEmbedding or YaRNScalingRotaryEmbedding instance, so layers sharing a configuration share one cos/sin cache.

nodes.s: Empty package marker for deepinfer.model_executor.layers.tilelang_ops, the TileLang execution layer that holds the backend dispatcher (ops.py) and the cuda/ and asc/ kernel backends.
Ascend (NPU) TileLang kernel that gathers a compact range of tokens out of the paged KV cache, handling the plain-bf16, quantized-index and FP4-cast cache layouts described by KVCacheFormat.

k.s: JIT-compiled Ascend kernel factory: specializes a paged-cache gather on the KVCacheFormat, block size and FP4 strides, then emits the T.prim_func that copies cache blocks into a contiguous output.

nodes.s: Single source of truth for KV-cache physical layouts: the KVCacheFormat dataclass, the five supported formats (V41 FP8/FP4 main cache and the FP4/FP8/MXFP8 index caches), allocation helpers and the torch reference casts the kernel tests compare against.

k.s: Frozen description of one KV-cache token: quantized dtype and element count, scale-factor format and granularity, bf16 tail, and the derived byte sizes and stride alignment every cache kernel is specialized on.
NamedTuple view splitting one cache buffer into its quantized data, scale-factor and bf16 sub-tensors.
Infers which supported KVCacheFormat a raw cache tensor uses from its bytes-per-token and scale format.
Normalizes the (cache tensor, explicit layout, sf_format) triple callers pass into one validated KVCacheFormat.
Allocates the destination tensors for a cache load — quantized data, scale factors in PLATFORM.fp8_sf_type, and an optional bf16 buffer — sized from the layout.
Allocates a paged KV cache of num_blocks x block_size tokens in the byte layout the format prescribes.
Slices a flat byte-typed cache buffer into the KVCacheTensors views (quantized data / scale factors / bf16).
Torch reference that quantizes bf16 tokens into the format's cache encoding, used as ground truth in the cache kernel tests.
Torch reference that dequantizes a cache token back to bf16, the inverse of ref_cast_from_bf16.
Parametrized check that every supported format's derived byte sizes and alignments are self-consistent.
Builds the kernel keyword arguments describing the FP4 KV-cache layout (block geometry, scale packing) shared by the store and load cache kernels, so both agree on one layout description.

nodes.s: Host-side ops for the sparse-attention candidate-block pipeline — per-block max scoring, compaction of the selected blocks and restoring compact indices to absolute token indices — each paired with a torch reference and pytest parity plus benchmark tests.

k.s: Reduces a [rows, max_model_len] score matrix to per-block maxima plus a valid-block count, capping at the largest finite bf16 and forcing +inf on the last valid block so it is always selected.
Torch reference for candidate_block_max used as the parity oracle.
Counts how many tokens each row contributes once only the selected candidate blocks are kept, giving the compact layout's per-row lengths.
Rewrites compact within-candidate indices back into absolute token indices in place, applying the per-row block offsets.
Torch reference for restore_candidate_indices_inplace.
Parity test over block sizes and row counts comparing candidate_block_max against its torch reference.
Parity test for restore_candidate_indices_inplace with and without an output index offset.
Throughput benchmark for candidate_block_max across row counts, valid lengths and block sizes.
Throughput benchmark for get_candidate_compact_lens across row and top-k block counts.
Throughput benchmark for the in-place candidate-index restore.

nodes.s: Host-side ops for the V4 compressor: fold every compress_ratio consecutive (score, latent) pairs into one compressed KV token while carrying the rolling state through a per-sequence state cache, in both the prefill and the decode shape; shipped with torch references and pytest parity/benchmark tests.

k.s: Prefill compressor op: emits [total_compressed, dim] bf16 compressed KV and updates the fp32 state cache in place, optionally de-permuting CP-mirrored rows via mirror_cp_reverse_index.
Decode compressor op: produces one bf16 row per query token (zeros where the token does not close a compress block) and advances the per-sequence state cache.
Torch reference for the prefill compressor, including the CP de-permutation path.
Torch reference for the decode compressor.
Shared prefill test body: builds randomized sequences and state slots, runs kernel and reference and asserts both the compressed output and the mutated state cache match.
Shared decode test body covering MTP batch shapes and the probability that a token closes a compress block.
Builds the randomized prefill benchmark inputs (sequences, state cache, optional CP index).
Throughput benchmark for the prefill compressor across compress ratios, dims and CP-index presence.
Builds the randomized decode benchmark inputs, including whether every sequence compresses this step.
Throughput benchmark for the decode compressor across compress ratios, dims and MTP batch sizes.

nodes.s: One small fused op for the ZOS decode step: advance each sequence's seqlens_k by its query length and claw back the draft tokens the previous MTP step proposed but did not accept — all in place on GPU.

k.s: In-place GPU update seqlens_k[i] += seqlens_q[i] - (nextn - prev_num_accepted_tokens[remap[i]]), skipping the correction for fresh sequences (remap == -1).
Torch reference for the fused seqlens_k update.
Parity test over remap presence and nextn values comparing kernel and reference.
Throughput benchmark of the seqlens_k update across sequence counts.

nodes.s: CUDA (SM100) TileLang kernel that gathers a compact range of tokens out of the paged KV cache; the CUDA twin of the Ascend kernel of the same name, selected at runtime through the ops.py backend dispatcher.

k.s: JIT-compiled CUDA kernel factory that builds a compact-range paged-cache load specialized on the layout, block size and FP4 value/scale strides.

nodes.s: Two DFlash (speculative draft) ops with references and tests: the fused confidence head that scores whether to keep drafting, and the fused mean-reduce that writes hidden states into the draft model's input buffer.

k.s: Fused sigmoid(cat([hidden, markov_emb]) @ weight / temperature) producing the per-token fp32 draft confidence used to decide how far DFlash keeps speculating.
Torch reference for the fused confidence head.
Parity test over token counts, embedding widths and Markov-embedding ranks.
Throughput benchmark for the fused confidence head.
Fused mean-reduce over the hc-head dimension that writes straight into a strided view of the DFlash input buffer, avoiding a separate copy.
Parity test for dflash_input_store across token counts, widths and hc multipliers.
Throughput benchmark for the DFlash input store.

nodes.s: Refills the DFlash decode CUDA graph's captured input tensors in a single TileLang launch — live requests first, padding rows after — so a graph replay never needs a host-side loop of per-tensor copies.

k.s: Copies the whole MTPDecodeInput tensor bundle (positions, golden tokens, sampling params, seeds, MTP write slots) from src then padding into the graph-captured dst in one launch.
Torch reference performing the same src-then-padding fill tensor by tensor.
Flattens an MTPSamplingInput into the ordered tensor tuple the kernel expects.
Builds a randomized MTPSamplingInput of the requested row count for the tests.
Builds a randomized MTPDecodeInput, with or without the driver-rank fields.
Parity test covering driver/follower ranks and padded/unpadded destinations.
Throughput benchmark across source and destination request counts.

nodes.s: Index-translation op for FlashMLA sparse attention: rewrites the top-k logical token indices into physical paged-cache slots through block_tables, masking anything past the context length.

k.s: In-place map of [bsz, seqlen_q, topk] logical indices to physical KV-cache slots via block_tables, writing -1 for positions beyond context_lens.
Torch reference for the top-k index to cache-slot translation.
Builds randomized top-k indices, context lengths and block tables for the tests and benchmarks.
Throughput benchmark for convert_kv_index across batch sizes and top-k widths.

nodes.s: The sampler kernel's host side: one fused op applying temperature, top-p/top-k, log-softmax and optional sampling — including speculative-decoding rejection sampling against draft logprobs — plus a full torch reference and a statistical test suite (goodness-of-fit, zero-residual and signed-zero edge cases).

k.s: Single-launch logits pipeline returning processed logprobs and, when sampling is enabled, candidate tokens, verify accept decisions, selected draft logprobs and accept probabilities.
Torch reference reproducing the whole fused_sample contract, rejection sampling included.
Torch reference for the top-p / top-k truncation applied before log-softmax.
Synthesizes logits matrices from several distributions (uniform, peaked, heavy-tailed) to exercise the sampler across realistic shapes.
Builds the draft-side tensors (draft logprobs, draft token ids, read rows) that switch on reject sampling.
Asserts the returned logprobs really are the top-p/top-k truncated and renormalized distribution.
Enumerates the (batch, vocab, distribution, top-p/top-k, verify) parameter grid shared by tests and benchmarks.
Main correctness body: runs kernel and reference over one parameter set and compares logprobs, chosen tokens, accept decisions and accept probabilities.
Statistical check that the accepted-token distribution of rejection sampling matches the target distribution over many draws.
Edge case where the residual distribution is all zeros, so the sampler must still return a valid token.
Edge case guarding against -0.0 probabilities breaking the top-p/top-k and residual arithmetic.
Registry mapping test kind/case names to the check functions above, driving the parametrized entry point.
Parametrized pytest entry point dispatching into the registered correctness cases.
Throughput benchmark sweeping batch size, vocabulary size and top-p/top-k settings.

nodes.s: The biggest fusion in the execution layer: RMSNorm -> RoPE -> Hadamard -> FP8/FP4 cast -> paged-KV-cache store collapsed into one kernel launch, described by a set of optional *Args dataclasses, with a full torch reference and a parametrized correctness/benchmark suite.

k.s: RMSNorm stage parameters: the per-head_dim weight and epsilon.
RoPE stage parameters: positions, the fp32 cos/sin cache, rotary dim, NeoX flag, offset and conjugation.
Hadamard stage parameters — just the normalization scale.
Quantization stage parameters (KVCacheFormat, per-channel counts, scale rounding and format, cast-back flag), with from_cache_format deriving them straight from a cache layout.
Output selector for a caller-owned contiguous destination plus its scale-factor tensor.
Output selector that scatters the transformed rows into a 4D paged KV cache through slot_mapping, with an optional extra bf16 copy.
Test-matrix dataclass enumerating one fused-transform configuration (which stages run, head shapes, cache format, block size, strides, preallocation) and deriving its kernel arguments.
The fused op entry point: validates shapes and strides, resolves the cache layout, allocates or binds the outputs, and launches the kernel specialized on exactly the stages requested.
Torch reference running the same stages sequentially, the oracle the fused kernel is compared against.
Torch reference for the normalized Hadamard transform stage.
Allocates (or validates) the quantized output and scale-factor tensors for a cast configuration, restoring the single-head axis when the input was 2-D.
Materializes one _FusedTransformCase into concrete input tensors, caches and argument dataclasses.
Computes the bytes moved by a case so the benchmark can report achieved bandwidth — this fusion is memory-bound.
Allocates the paged KV cache a benchmark case stores into.
Deep-copies an out_args bundle so kernel and reference write into independent buffers.
Compares the kernel and reference results across the several possible return shapes.
Parity test running every stage combination in the case matrix against the torch reference.
Bandwidth benchmark over the case matrix and token counts.
