k.s: Dispatches the fused Engram n-gram gather, branching fresh vs. previous sequences inside the kernel via the remap table and rolling back rejected draft tokens using prev_num_accepted_tokens.
Torch reference spelling out the three-source lookback selection and the image-sentinel padding rule.
Parity test over nextn, n-gram order and the fraction of sequences carried over from the previous step.
Throughput benchmark of the Engram token gather across sequence counts.

nodes.s: Fills the decode step's input_ids on GPU: carried-over sequences read the previous step's sampled token and predicted draft tokens through the remap table, fresh sequences read their CPU-supplied tokens.

k.s: Dispatches the input_ids gather kernel over the varlen query layout defined by seqlens_q / cu_seqlens_q.
Torch reference for the fresh-vs-previous input_ids selection.
Parity test over nextn and the fraction of carried-over sequences.
Throughput benchmark of the input_ids gather across sequence counts.

nodes.s: Index-preparation ops for V4 attention: materializing the compressed-attention and sliding-window KV index tensors for prefill and decode, plus get_fused_dflash_get_input, which builds every DFlash draft-token input (slot mapping, positions, masks and KV index) in one launch.

k.s: Expands per-row (offset, len) pairs into the prefill compressed-attention KV index, padding with -1.
Torch reference for the prefill compressed-attention index expansion.
Decode variant that additionally translates logical offsets into physical cache slots through block_tables.
Torch reference for the decode compressed-attention index expansion.
Builds the decode sliding-window KV index, wrapping offsets inside the ring-buffer SWA cache block.
Torch reference for the decode sliding-window index.

One kernel producing all six DFlash draft-token inputs — new-token SWA store slots, positions, zeroed input_ids, valid-token and gate masks, and the padded KV index — with CUDA-graph padding rows masked out.
Torch reference building the same six DFlash draft-token tensors step by step.
Builds randomized real and padding request inputs for the DFlash index tests.
Parity test for the three KV-index ops across row counts, index lengths, block sizes and modes.
Parity test for the fused DFlash input build, covering padding requests and the optional mask outputs.
Throughput benchmark for the fused DFlash input build.
Combined benchmark driver for the KV-index ops across modes.
Benchmark for the decode compressed-attention index expansion.
Benchmark for the decode sliding-window index expansion.
Benchmark for the prefill compressed-attention index expansion.

nodes.s: mHC runtime for the V4.1 backbone: HCLayerMixin expands the residual into an hc_mult-way trunk, mixes it into each sub-layer input (pre) and folds the sub-layer output back (post), with a single-call deep_gemm.mega_mhc fusion on GPU; HCHead collapses the trunk back to one hidden state before the lm head.

k.s: NamedTuple bundling one sub-layer's HC parameters (fn matrix, sigmoid scales, mix bases) with its layer norm, so the attn and ffn paths can share the same pre/post code.

Runs the mHC pre/post mixing pair around attention and FFN: post of the previous sub-layer, pre of this one and the layer norm (plus FP8 cast) are carried back to back, fused into one deep_gemm.mega_mhc call when hc_mult is 4 and the fn hidden is split-K align

Final mHC step before the lm head: mixes the hc_mult-way residual trunk back into single-path hidden states via `mhc_head`. Not built for shifted-HC checkpoints, which instead apply the last sub-layer's pre mix.

nodes.s: FP32 mHC parameter containers in HF checkpoint layout: mixins that declare the per-block and per-head base/fn/scale tensors, plus MoeDecoderBlockHC, the V4.1 backbone block that wires MLA attention, the fused MoE experts and the HC parameters together.

k.s: Declares one block's HC parameters in HF layout: the (2 + m) * m base vector seeded from the pre/post/res init values, the FP32 fn matrices for attn and ffn (norm weights already folded in) and their dynamic scales, plus weightless norm holders that only carry
Declares the non-shifted HC head tensors in the folded HF layout: the per-head layer mix vector, the FP32 transposed fn matrix with norm weights folded into its columns, and a scalar scale.

One V4.1 backbone block as a container with stable HF parameter paths: MLA attention, two RMSNorms, the fused MoE experts, the HC parameters and an optional Engram embedding; asserts that HC is enabled and dynamic.

nodes.s: Dependency-free dataclass carrying the HC residual trunk plus the pre/post/comb mixing coefficients from `_hc_pre` to the paired `hc_post`, kept free of imports so the YoCo operator layer can inspect and rebuild it without pulling in the fused kernel stack.

k.s: Per-token bundle of the HC residual trunk and its post / comb / pre mixing coefficients; `clear_post` releases the consumed post fields while keeping the pre mix that the next shifted-HC sub-layer still needs.

nodes.s: HF parameter containers for the output heads: GPTHead (final norm + lm head), MarkovGPTHead adding a first-order Markov logit correction, the DFlash acceptance-rate predictor, and the HC-aware main and draft prediction heads.

k.s: Output norm plus the vocab-sized lm head projection, kept in bf16.
Final DFlash head adding a first-order Markov correction to the logits via a low-rank token embedding and a second vocab projection.
DFlash acceptance-rate head: a single projection to one scalar per token, used to predict how likely a draft token is accepted.
Main model prediction head wrapping GPTHead; builds HC head parameters only for non-shifted checkpoints, since shifted HC is completed by the final block's pre mix.

One DFlash draft block: the first shift adds the token embedding, the projection over the concatenated target-layer hidden states and its norm; the last shift adds the Markov lm head, the acceptance-rate head and (non-shifted HC only) the HC head parameters.

nodes.s: Two nn.Linear subclasses used purely as HF parameter containers: ReplicatedLinear for complete weights and ParallelRoutedLinear for expert-major grouped-GEMM weights, both tagging whether the weight participates in FP8/FP4 GEMM.

k.s: nn.Linear holding a complete (unsharded) weight, tagged with whether it takes part in FP8 GEMM so meta materialization can prepare the quantized layout.
nn.Linear holding this rank's routed expert weights in the expert-major (n_local_experts * h_in, h_out) grouped-GEMM layout; HF materialization writes packed FP4 straight into it.

nodes.s: Two inference-only compositions over the mHC operators: `mhc_head` chains prenorm GEMM, head mix and apply-mix for the lm head, and `mhc_pre_big_fuse` hands the split-K GEMM partials straight to the fused tile-kernels epilogue.

k.s: mHC processing for the final lm head: pads the head fn matrix to the block fn shape to reuse the prenorm-GEMM kernel, computes the head mix and applies it, collapsing the trunk to the hidden state fed to the lm head.

Fused inference-only mHC pre path: calls the split-K prenorm GEMM directly and lets one tile-kernels epilogue do reduce + RMSNorm + split mixes + Sinkhorn + apply mix, returning the post mix, comb mix and the sub-layer input.

nodes.s: Tensor-shaping wrappers around the prebuilt tile_kernels mHC kernels (expand, post, pre-apply-mix, head mix, split mixes, Sinkhorn, prenorm GEMM) that allocate the output buffers and flatten views; the split-K count differs per platform (Ascend reduces inside the kernel, CUDA needs 16 partials).

k.s: Split-K count for the prenorm GEMM, the one platform fork in this file: 1 on Ascend (the kernel reduces internally) and 16 on CUDA (the partials are reduced by the epilogue).
Broadcasts a single-path hidden state into the hc_mult-way residual trunk used by the first HC layer.
Writes a sub-layer output back into the residual trunk using the post and comb mixes computed by the paired pre step.
Reduces the hc_mult-way trunk to one bf16 hidden state with a per-path mix vector - the apply half of the HC pre step.
Turns the head's raw prenorm-GEMM mixes into the sigmoid-scaled per-path mix used by the lm-head collapse.
Splits the concatenated mix vector produced by the prenorm GEMM into the pre, post and comb-residual mixes and reshapes them to the per-token layouts the post kernel expects.
Sinkhorn-normalizes the hc_mult x hc_mult combination matrix so the trunk mixing stays doubly stochastic.
Runs the TF32 prenorm GEMM from DeepGEMM over the flattened trunk, returning the split-K partial products and their squared sums for the RMSNorm epilogue.
Unfused PolyNorm mix computation: optionally merges the norm weight into the fn matrix, runs the split-K prenorm GEMM and reduces the partials with an RMSNorm epilogue.

nodes.s: HF parameter containers for one V4.1 attention layer: the MLA low-rank Wq/Wkv projections, the gated compressed-KV projection, the MQA sparse indexer, and LoraRopeCompressFlashMHAAutoRecomp which assembles them and holds the module only on layers that are KV / index sources.

k.s: MLA low-rank projection container `x -> A -> (norm) -> B`; with out_features == 0 only A exists, which is how Wkv produces the compressed KV plus its RoPE heads.

Compressed-KV projection container: A produces the values and Gate the softmax logits; the gate is omitted at compression ratio 1, where a single-token softmax is always 1. Both stay bf16 and out of FP8 quantization.

Sparse-attention indexer container (the use_kproj variant): the q_B / weights_proj / k_proj projections, an optional k norm and its own rotary embedding, which score tokens so attention only reads the index_topk candidates.

Full parameter container of one V4.1 attention layer: MLA Wq/Wkv/Wv/out_proj, the grouped V projection with its einsum layout, the compressed-KV PackedWkv and the MQA indexer (held only on source layers), the rotary embedding and the optional per-head attentio

nodes.s: MoE runtime: DeepseekMoE converts the FusedExperts container into the runtime expert layout and implements EPLB-aware gating, DeepEP dispatch/combine, grouped FP8/FP4 expert GEMMs with a fused SwiGLU epilogue, and the single-kernel mega-MoE path used inside an NVLink domain.

k.s: Repacks an HF expert weight into the runtime expert-major layout and converts its scale factors: FP4-QAT checkpoints are re-cast to packed e2m1 with TMA-aligned column-major scales, FP8 ones go through DeepGEMM's required scale layout; the source storage is fr
Transforms a pair of expert weights (and their scale factors) into the mega-MoE kernel layout and releases the source storage.
Dispatches one grouped expert GEMM to DeepGEMM - FP8 x FP8/FP4 or bf16 - using the psum layout keyed by the per-expert received-token counts.

Runtime MoE layer: builds the EPLB physical-expert mapping, gates tokens with the mega-gate or the TileKernels top-k gate, then either runs the fused single-kernel mega-MoE over a symmetric buffer or the DeepEP dispatch, grouped expert GEMM with fused SwiGLU,

nodes.s: HF parameter containers for the MoE block: routed FusedExperts with the logical / extra / physical / local expert accounting shared with EPLB, the sqrtsoftplus + noaux_tc TopKGate carrying separate text and image routing biases, and the shared expert concatenated along the hidden dim.

k.s: Shared-expert container: the n_shared_experts are concatenated along the hidden dim into one pair of linears instead of separate submodules.
Top-k routing gate container: a bf16 gate projection plus two FP32 load-correction biases (text and image); asserts sqrtsoftplus scoring, noaux_tc selection and top-k probability normalization.
Container for this rank's routed experts, shared experts and gate; derives the physical expert count from logical plus redundant experts and splits it evenly over the expert-parallel group.

nodes.s: DropoutAddRMSNorm parameter container holding hidden size, epsilon, optional exponential weight and output scale; it deliberately has no forward, `utils.convert_rmsnorm` turns it into the runtime RMSNorm.

k.s: Parameter-only RMSNorm container: keeps hidden size, epsilon, output scale and an optional weight (exponentiated when the checkpoint stores log-space norm weights), exposing `get_weight` for the runtime conversion.

nodes.s: Parameter-free RoPE hyperparameter containers (base and YaRN) plus `build_rotary_emb`, which selects one by config; `utils.convert_rope` later builds the runtime rotary embedding and its cos/sin cache from them.

k.s: Parameter-free container for base / position-interpolation RoPE, holding only the base frequency and whether the layout is interleaved.
YaRN RoPE container adding the original context length, the extension factor, the beta_fast/beta_slow correction range and the mscale flags.
Builds the RoPE container matching the configured variant (base or yarn) without warming up the cos/sin cache; any other variant raises.

nodes.s: Container-to-runtime conversions for the V4.1 model: RoPE and RMSNorm adapters, linear-weight merging with FP8 scale factors, chunked on-GPU dummy-weight initialization for huge CPU tables, and the decoder-layer registry that drives timer sampling groups.

k.s: Converts a RoPE container into the runtime rotary embedding, translating a YaRN container into the rope_scaling dict that `get_rope` expects and mapping the interleaved flag to neox style.

Concatenates several linear weights into one parameter, also concatenating their FP8 scale factors and requiring every segment but the last to be a multiple of 128; the source storages are freed in place.
Generates random weights for large CPU tables in bounded 16M-element GPU chunks and copies each chunk back, avoiding minutes of CPU-side bf16 generation and FP8 conversion for the Engram tables.
Seeds a parameter for dummy-weight runs: FP8/FP4 weights get random bytes with a neutral scale factor, floating-point weights a normal distribution, and integer weights zeros.
Converts a DropoutAddRMSNorm container into the runtime RMSNorm, carrying over the effective weight, epsilon, output scale and FP8 flag.
Registers a layer index under its structural key in the two module-level registries that group identical decoder layers for timer sampling.
Returns the second and second-to-last layer of the group a layer belongs to, plus the whole group - the layers chosen to carry timers so warm-up and tail effects are excluded.

nodes.s: YoCo prefill-truncation predicates and runtime operations: decides which layers are consumers and whether the shared hidden must be carried across layers, and compacts hidden states, HC lazy data and cross-layer index caches at the truncation boundary, gathering across context-parallel ranks when CP is on.

k.s: Decides whether the YoCo shared hidden (the attn-norm hidden of the first consumer layer) has to be captured and passed on, by checking for later consumer layers that project SWA KV from it or recompute packed KV as a KV source.

Compacts a per-token tensor at the YoCo truncation boundary: a plain gather by query index without context parallelism, otherwise select-contributed, all-gather in rank order through the CP user buffer, and select this rank's post-compaction share.
Applies the boundary compaction to every per-token field of an HCLazyPostData bundle, returning a compact copy of the HC trunk and its mixes.

Rearranges all boundary state at once - hidden states, the residual or HC lazy bundle, and the cross-layer top-k / candidate-block indices - invalidates the derived candidate caches, and returns both the compact copies and the original full tensors.

nodes.s: CPManager wraps a DeepEP BucketBuffer as context-parallel communication storage: scoped sessions, in-place shard allocation, and an asynchronous all_gather whose wait callback concatenates the rank shards along the token axis.

k.s: Owns the context-parallel DeepEP BucketBuffer: opens one session at a time, hands out this rank's contiguous shard of a gathered region, and launches all_gather returning a wait callback that views the result as tokens concatenated across ranks. Gathered tenso

nodes.s: Process-wide `userbuffer` singleton owning every communication buffer of one loaded model - the DeepEP EPBuffer, the CP BucketBuffer, the Engram RDMA buffer and cached DeepGEMM SymmBuffer views - plus `limit_num_sms`, which temporarily reserves SMs for communication.

k.s: NamedTuple identity of one DeepGEMM SymmBuffer view whose fields are exactly the SymmBuffer kwargs, used as the cache key so equal specs share one instance.
Context manager that lowers the SM budget of both TileKernels and DeepGEMM by num_sms for its body and restores it afterwards, so compute does not contend with the communication kernels.

Allocates and owns every process-wide communication buffer for one model: the DeepEP EPBuffer (also deriving the communication SM count), the CP BucketBuffer, the Engram RDMA buffer with CPU or GPU storage, and a cache of DeepGEMM SymmBuffer views sharing the

nodes.s: vLLM-derived model-executor helpers, trimmed by DeepSeek to four: RNG seeding, parameter reconstruction that isolates per-model parameter lifetimes, an environment-variable integer-range parser, and a move-only `Movable` ownership wrapper.

k.s: Seeds Python, NumPy and Torch (including all CUDA devices) from one value.
Rebuilds an nn.Parameter over the same storage (carrying its FP8 scale factor) so two models can hold the same tensor without one being freed when the other is released.
Parses an environment-variable integer set like '0..3,7,10..12' into a list, requiring strictly increasing segments and a value range, with Chinese error messages naming the offending variable.
Move-only wrapper mimicking C++ std::move: `move()` hands ownership to the callee and empties the wrapper, so a second move raises instead of keeping a large tensor alive.

nodes.s: vLLM-derived cache engine reworked for V4.1's heterogeneous KV: StateBlock and KVCacheManager compute the per-layer byte layout of compressed KV, sparse-index KV, SWA rings and FP32 compression state (honoring share-kv / share-index reuse and the YoCo stored/dropped split), GPUCacheInterface carves the views and moves state to disk or to the completion engine, and CacheEngine allocates the GPU buffers.

k.s: Returns the per-token interleaved KV cache size (data plus scale) from the V41 or V41-FP4 cache format, asserting the config's element and scale granularity match that format.
Evaluates a per-layer indexer property across every attention layer that has an attn_index config and asserts they all agree, returning 0 when no layer has one.
SWA ring size from the kvstore's point of view: the inference window plus the extra tokens needed because persistence only happens at 128-token boundaries, plus the YoCo anchor rollback margin.

Generic share-kv / share-index resolution: returns which earlier layer's cache this layer reuses according to the named map in layer_info_shared_cfg, defaulting to itself and asserting the target was already processed.
Resolves which layer's indexer K cache this layer uses, preferring the dedicated index-K map and otherwise following the index-module map, so index K sharing stays decoupled from main KV sharing.
Yields the compression layers that actually own FP32 state, flagging separately whether they own the main and the index state rather than reusing another layer's.

Per-layer bundle of cache views: the sparse index KV and its FP32 state, the compressed attention KV and its state, and the sliding-window ring - any of which is None when the layer does not use or does not own that cache.

Computes the byte layout of one sequence's state slot: persisted SWA rings first, then the dropped region of YoCo-consumer SWA and FP32 compression state, so writing to disk is a length truncation; handles per-layer 32-byte padding and the lcm alignment the SW

Walks the attention layers in runtime order and carves each layer's index KV, compressed KV, SWA ring and compression-state views out of the flat uint8 buffers, advancing 32-byte-aligned offsets, skipping layers that reuse another layer's cache, and finally cr

Per-layer access to the carved caches plus the class-level layout description used to move state: carves parallel kvstore and inference views, selects the slice to persist at a 128-token boundary (re-ringing when extra state is kept), and loads a stored state

Allocates the GPU KV and state buffers through the C++ cuda_utils allocator after computing the block shape and layout, logs the padding overhead and buffer sizes, and exposes the pure sizing helpers the profiler calls before any allocation.

nodes.s: Pytest unit test for `_UserBufferManager` with a faked DeepGEMM SymmBuffer: asserts that equal specs return one shared instance, that smaller specs become views of the first base, and that `close()` destroys views before their base and is idempotent.

k.s: Test helper allocating a SymmBuffer through the manager with a fixed expert/hidden spec and only max_num_tokens varying.
Asserts the first allocated spec owns the storage, an identical spec returns the same instance, and smaller specs come back as views whose base is that first buffer.
Asserts `close()` destroys the EP, CP and Engram buffers, destroys SymmBuffer views before their base, empties their attribute dicts, clears the manager's references and can be called twice safely.

nodes.s: Multimodal vision pre/post-processing ops: scatters ViT embeddings into the text embedding stream at image-token positions, turns raw packed HWC RGB bytes into normalized bf16 patches on GPU, and spatially downsamples ViT patch features. Each op pairs a TileLang-backed wrapper with a PyTorch reference and pytest correctness/benchmark cases.

k.s: In-place scatter of ViT embeddings into the text embedding stream: the i-th image token receives images_embeds[i], and each image-pad token id gets its own learned pad embedding. Computes the inclusive prefix sum of image-token occurrences and hands it to ops.
PyTorch reference for replace_input_embeds, used by the pytest correctness cases to pin the scatter semantics.

Converts concatenated plain HWC uint8 RGB bytes into normalized bf16 patch tensors, center-padding each real image into its n_vit grid on the GPU so the CPU worker can forward ImageOps.contain output verbatim.
PyTorch reference for rgb_pad_to_patches, reproducing the per-image center pad, normalization and patchification.

Per-image d x d spatial downsample of ViT patch features, either channel-concatenating the window (downsample_mlp_gelu / identity) or mean-pooling it, with zero crop rows treated as cached-image dummies.
PyTorch reference for batch_downsample covering both the channel-concat and mean-pool modes.
Synthesizes the input_ids / embeddings / pad-token fixtures the image-embed tests and benchmarks run on, given a token count, hidden size and image layout.
Parametrized correctness test comparing the rgb_pad_to_patches kernel against its PyTorch reference across padded and unpadded crop layouts.

nodes.s: Concatenates the sliding-window KV index with the sparse compressed-attention index into one per-query index row, rebasing the second half by total_k_swa + total_k while preserving -1 padding. Memory-bound gather-index prep with a PyTorch reference and pytest cases.

k.s: Concatenates the per-query sliding-window KV index with the sparse compressed-attention index, rebasing the latter by total_k_swa + total_k while keeping -1 padding, and returns a stride-padded (possibly non-contiguous) view.
PyTorch reference for kv_index_cat built from torch.cat plus a where() that preserves -1 entries.

nodes.s: Single format-inferred API for gathering compact physical block ranges out of the paged KV cache, covering plain BF16 layouts and quantized (FP8/FP4 + scale-factor) layouts with optional cast-to-BF16. Dispatches to ops.load_paged_kv_cache_tl and ships a PyTorch reference plus layout-parametrized pytest cases.

k.s: Loads compact physical block ranges out of the paged KV cache through one layout-inferred API, covering plain BF16 caches and quantized caches with scale factors, with optional cast-to-BF16 and an Ascend-specific batching heuristic for large mostly-full page s
PyTorch reference for load_paged_kv_cache, reproducing segment gathering, zero-fill for src_block_id == -1 and the dequantization paths for every supported layout.
Layout- and segment-pattern-parametrized correctness test that stores through store_kv_cache_ref, loads back through the kernel and compares against the reference loader.

nodes.s: RMSNorm forward with optional fused residual-add and fused FP8 cast, covering every scale-factor layout the downstream GEMMs want (row-major, TMA-aligned column-major, packed UE8M0, and the mega-MoE shared_l1_acts_sf layout). Includes the scale-factor allocator, a PyTorch reference and heavy pytest coverage.

k.s: RMSNorm forward with optional fused residual-add and fused FP8 cast. A single entry point covers every scale-factor layout the downstream GEMMs need -- row-major, TMA-aligned column-major, packed UE8M0 and the mega-MoE shared_l1_acts_sf layout -- and returns a
PyTorch reference for the RMSNorm forward, including the residual add performed in the input dtype before float32 norm statistics.

Allocates the FP8 scale-factor tensor for a norm+cast, returning both the caller-facing view and the kernel argument view; handles row-major, packed UE8M0 and TMA-aligned column-major layouts with their differing padding rules.

The main correctness test for norm: sweeps hidden sizes, residual presence and output forms, and checks both the normalized output and every scale-factor layout against the reference using assert_close.

nodes.s: The 32-line kernel dispatcher for the whole TileLang layer: imports the backend package named by PLATFORM.tilelang_ops_backend (cuda or asc), re-exports every *_tl kernel factory it finds, and raises KernelUnavailableError for kernels the selected backend lacks. Backend selection happens only here.

k.s: AttributeError subclass raised when the selected TileLang backend has no factory for a requested kernel; conftest.py converts it into a test skip on non-CUDA backends while keeping the hasattr / module __getattr__ protocol intact.

nodes.s: Debug guard that queues an asynchronous device-side assertion for NaN, infinity, or values outside +/-1e11 in any activation tensor. Thin wrapper over ops.detect_outlier_and_abort_tl; one of the few top-level tilelang_ops modules with no pytest cases.

k.s: Queues an asynchronous device-side assertion that aborts on NaN, infinity, or absolute values above 1e11 anywhere in a tensor, printing the caller-supplied id, the fp32 value and the flat element offset on failure.

nodes.s: Builds the mirror context-parallel token mapping: the forward/reverse index that assigns each rank its mirrored half of every sequence, plus per-compression-ratio key start/end bounds, and the fused YOCO CP boundary computation. Both CUDA and Ascend share one TileLang entry.

k.s: Builds the mirror context-parallel index pair (forward index of this rank's tokens and the reverse index back to global order) plus per-compression-ratio key start/end bounds, in one TileLang entry shared by both backends with an output-parallel scatter.
PyTorch reference for prepare_cp_mirror that constructs the mirrored per-rank token assignment and key bounds from plain sequence lengths.
Computes the YOCO context-parallel boundary metadata in one fused kernel: per-rank contribution offsets and padded lengths over the compressed query sequence.
PyTorch reference for the YOCO CP boundary computation, used to pin the padded contribution lengths.

nodes.s: Computes the entire V4 decode-step metadata bundle in one TileLang launch (one CTA per sequence): compacted block tables, per-ratio positions and slot mappings, SWA and compressed-attention index offsets, state block indices, routing masks and query indices. A ~175-line PyTorch reference and a 136-line correctness test pin the semantics.

k.s: Computes the whole V4 decode-step metadata bundle on device with one CTA per sequence plus a second kernel to expand block_tables_out: compacted block tables, per-ratio positions and slot mappings, SWA and compressed-attention index offsets, state block indice
The ~175-line PyTorch reference that defines the exact semantics of every output of prepare_v4_decode_metadata, including the per-ratio bucketing and placeholder-sequence handling.
Exhaustive correctness test sweeping placeholder sequences, query lengths, block-table sizes and ratio sets, comparing every metadata output tensor against the reference.

nodes.s: Batch-invariant weighted sampler: picks one vocabulary column per row from a probability matrix using a hash of (seq_seed, sample_position) rather than a shared RNG stream, so results do not depend on batch size or row order. Backed by a goodness-of-fit test plus degenerate, extreme-scale and batch-invariance cases.

k.s: Samples one vocabulary column per row weighted by probs, deriving randomness from a hash of (seq_seed, sample_position) so the result is independent of batch size and row order; zero-probability columns are never selected.
PyTorch reference for the batch-invariant sampler, reproducing the per-row hash-to-uniform draw and the inclusive-CDF search.
Correctness test over several probability distributions and batch shapes, checking the kernel matches the reference draw for identical seeds and positions.
Statistical goodness-of-fit test: draws millions of samples per distribution and checks the empirical frequencies match the target probabilities, catching bias that an exact-match test cannot.

nodes.s: Distributes a fixed total_q query-token budget across sequences according to the previous step's multi-token-prediction confidence rates, fusing the remap scatter that carries confidences over from the previous batch. Sequences with higher accepted-draft confidence get longer speculative query lengths.

k.s: Distributes a fixed total_q query-token budget across sequences in proportion to the previous step's multi-token-prediction confidence rates, fusing the remap scatter that carries confidences over from the previous batch.
PyTorch reference for the MTP-confidence query-length scheduler, spelling out the remap, the cumulative-rate ordering and the integer budget allocation.

nodes.s: Moves the compressor's rolling state window between the circular per-layer state cache and the inference-sized state tensor: select_state_slice gathers the window ending at last_hit_position, load_state_to_cache writes it back. Both are modulo-indexed copies with PyTorch references and pytest cases.

k.s: Gathers the state window ending at last_hit_position out of the circular per-layer state cache into the inference-sized state tensor, indexing each side modulo its own block size.
Writes the inference-sized state tensor back into the circular per-layer state cache at the window ending at last_hit_position, the inverse of select_state_slice.

nodes.s: Single format-inferred API for scattering BF16 tokens into the paged KV cache by slot mapping, quantizing on the way in for FP8/FP4 layouts and skipping -1 padding slots. The reference path carries two Ascend workarounds for torch_npu's IndexPutV2 32-bit offset wraparound and for slot-0 padding aliasing.

k.s: Scatters BF16 tokens into the paged KV cache by slot mapping through one layout-inferred API, quantizing on the way in for FP8/FP4 layouts and skipping -1 padding slots; the NPU path reshapes the cache directly instead of going through split_kv_cache.
PyTorch reference store path, also reused by the load_paged_kv_cache tests to populate a cache before reading it back.
Performs cache[block, offset] = values, falling back on Ascend to a flat 64-bit as_strided index_put_ because torch_npu's IndexPutV2 wraps around at 32-bit offsets.

Reference-path masked scatter that clamps negative slots, writes through _slot_scatter, and then repairs slot 0 -- which multiple padding tokens can alias -- by restoring either the first real value or the original contents.
Layout-, block-size- and slot-pattern-parametrized correctness test for the store path, including padding slots and the guarded alignment variants.

Guarded entry point around the KV-cache store kernel: validates layout/dtype preconditions before dispatching the TileLang store, so a mismatched cache layout fails loudly instead of corrupting blocks.

nodes.s: Writes one contiguous nextn-sized block of speculative-decoding bookkeeping per request into the MTP pools: draft token ids, logprobs, optional logprob indices and per-position confidence. Slot 0 is reserved padding and writes targeting it are skipped.

k.s: Writes one contiguous nextn-sized block of speculative-decoding state per request into the MTP pools -- draft token ids, logprobs, optional logprob indices and per-position confidence -- skipping writes aimed at the reserved padding slot 0.
PyTorch reference for the MTP pool write, including the slot-0 skip and the optional index/confidence pools.
Correctness test over the optional-index, vocabulary-size and confidence combinations, verifying pool contents and that slot 0 stays untouched.

nodes.s: Computes the inclusive CDF value at the sampled token: per row, the sum of probabilities of all tokens with smaller probability plus equal-probability tokens up to the sampled column. Feeds speculative-decoding acceptance math; negative sample results yield 0.

k.s: Returns, per row, the inclusive CDF value at the sampled token: the summed probability of every strictly smaller-probability token plus equal-probability tokens up to the sampled column. Negative sample results produce 0.
PyTorch reference for the inclusive-CDF reduction, making the column-index tie-break explicit.

nodes.s: Expands the two per-token KV segments of sliding-window attention (offset/length pairs) into a dense [num_tokens, width] index matrix into the gathered KV buffer, padding unused columns with -1 and clipping over-long segments.

k.s: Expands the two per-token KV segments of sliding-window attention (offset/length pairs packed as int32 [num_tokens, 4]) into a dense [num_tokens, width] index matrix, clipping long segments and filling unused columns with -1.
PyTorch reference for the SWA index expansion built from arange comparisons and two torch.where branches.

nodes.s: Compressed-KV runtime for DeepSeek-V4: Compressor runs the gated low-rank KV compression plus RMSNorm, returns the pre-RoPE latent that feeds the sparse indexer, and stores the post-RoPE value into the main paged KV cache through the fused norm/RoPE/Hadamard/cast/store kernel. KProject projects that latent to the indexer's K.

k.s: The sparse indexer's K projection: a ReplicatedLinear over the post-norm pre-RoPE compressed latent followed by RMSNorm. Index-K normalization for the cache path lives in index_attn.py instead.

The pure KV compressor for V4: runs the gated low-rank compression (C1 or C2) with prefill/decode-specific TileLang state updates, applies RMSNorm, returns the pre-RoPE latent the indexer needs, and stores the post-RoPE value into the paged KV cache via the fu

nodes.s: The sparse-attention indexer: MQA computes relu(q@k)*weights logits against the FP4 index-KV cache and selects the top-k compressed KV blocks per query, handling separate prefill and decode metadata paths, candidate-block restriction, chunked logit computation under a memory budget, and cross-layer index-K sharing.

k.s: The sparse-attention indexer module: scores compressed KV with relu(q@k)*weights against an FP4 index-KV cache and selects the top-k blocks per query, with separate prefill and decode metadata paths, candidate-block restriction, chunked logit computation under
Pads the indexer weight rows to the 16-byte stride deep_gemm requires while leaving the logical head count unchanged, copying into a fresh zero buffer only when the existing stride is unaligned.

nodes.s: Two-function numerical comparison helper used by the kernel test suite: cal_diff reports cosine difference, RMSE, Chebyshev distance and a KL-like term between two tensors, and assert_close fails on NaNs or a cosine difference above eps.

k.s: Computes cosine difference, RMSE, Chebyshev distance and a KL-like term between two tensors in float64, short-circuiting to zeros when the tensors are bit-identical.
Kernel-test assertion helper: rejects NaNs, zeroes non-finite entries, prints all four difference metrics and fails when cosine difference exceeds eps.

nodes.s: Ascend NPU TileLang kernel that fuses the whole sampling tail into one pass over the logits: temperature-softmax, top-p/top-k filtering and plain or reject sampling, reusing the two-level sampler primitives from the sibling random_sampling module.

k.s: Picks the largest 64-aligned chunk that divides vocab_size and still fits the per-vector-core UB budget, so the log-sum-exp reduction order matches the reference implementation.
SIMD macro that folds one chunk of probabilities into quartile sums and counts, feeding the 16-round binary search that locates the top-p / top-k cutoff without a full sort.

JIT factory for the fused sampling kernel, specialized on vocab_size and the do_sample / do_reject_sampling switches; emits the softmax, threshold-search, masking and sampling stages as one NPU kernel and optionally returns logprobs for speculative decoding.

nodes.s: Ascend NPU megakernel running the full post-projection transform — RMSNorm, RoPE, Hadamard rotation, FP8/FP4 cast and paged KV-cache store — in a single SIMD pipeline so hidden states are read from HBM only once.

k.s: The actual prim_func pipeline, specialized by ~36 compile-time descriptors that switch each stage (norm / rope / hadamard / cast / store) and pin the register and DMA schedule.
Public JIT factory translating the backend-neutral fused-transform ABI into the Ascend kernel's compile-time descriptors (head burst, SIMD head count, scale-factor format, cache layout).

nodes.s: Register-only BF16 to FP8/FP4 KV quantization primitives for Ascend SIMD: grouped amax reduction, exact reciprocal scales via a lookup table, and sticky-bit FP4 packing. Callers own the masks and UB/GM layout.

k.s: Materializes the 8-entry e4m3 reciprocal lookup table into one vector register, so dequant scales can be recovered with a register shuffle instead of a divide.
Builds the macro that encodes per-group maxima as e4m3 scale bytes and returns their exact FP32 inverses, optionally through the reciprocal LUT.

Builds the paired compute_scales / quantize_value macros that turn two FP32 registers holding 128 BF16 values into FP8 bytes or packed FP4 nibbles plus encoded scales, with variants for sparse group-32 scales and packed main-cache rows.

nodes.s: Ascend NPU RMSNorm kernel with optional residual add, output scaling and fused FP8 cast with per-channel scale factors; the memory-bound norm that precedes every attention and MLP block.

k.s: Loads an even/odd FP32 register pair from a BF16 or FP32 buffer, unpacking BF16 lanes with a single vector convert.
Writes an even/odd register pair back to a buffer, packing to BF16 when the destination is BF16.
Chooses how many rows one UB tile holds given hidden_size and input dtype, balancing DMA burst length against buffer capacity.
JIT factory for the Ascend RMSNorm kernel, specialized on hidden size, dtypes, residual/FP8 switches and all sequence-direction strides; shares the compensated RSTD macro with fused_transform.

nodes.s: Two-level fixed-point weighted sampler for Ascend: a row is folded into acc_slots partial sums, an inclusive CDF picks a slot, then a second search resolves the exact column. Shared by the standalone sampling kernel and by fused_sample.

k.s: Frozen dataclass holding the compile-time sampling layout (vocab_size, threads, chunk width bd, acc_slots fold factor and fixed-point scale) plus the derived chunk/slot counts.
Folds a bd-wide chunk of probabilities (or log-probs) into the acc_slots fixed-point accumulators indexed by column modulo acc_slots, optionally also capturing draft log-probs.
In-place inclusive prefix scan over a multiple of 64 elements inside a SIMD vector frame, carrying sums across 64-element segments; also handles uint16-packed count prefixes.
Binary-searches a CDF buffer for the first entry strictly greater than the target, the primitive both sampling levels use to turn a random draw into an index.
Coarse level: maps the random target into one of the acc_slots lanes using the accumulated CDF.
Fine level: scans the candidate columns of the chosen slot with the remaining random mass and writes the selected token id for the row.
Derives the uniform draw for a row from the per-sequence seed and position hash, so sampling is reproducible and distinct across speculative-decoding steps.
JIT factory for the standalone Ascend sampler, specialized on vocab_size and whether the call comes from the next-n (MTP) predictor path.

nodes.s: Compensated reciprocal-standard-deviation for Ascend, matching hai_llm's rstd_1ulp to within one ULP. Shared by norm and fused_transform so both inference paths keep the training stack's FP32 FMA operation order.

k.s: Splits a Python float into high and low FP32 parts whose sum approximates it, the host-side half of the double-FP32 scheme.
Refines an rsqrt estimate with one Newton step evaluated against both the high and low parts of its input, recovering the squaring error with fused multiply-adds.
Computes a / c0 + c1 in double-FP32, returning high and low parts; the variance-plus-epsilon step of RMSNorm done without losing low-order bits.
Builds the compensated RSTD macro for a given hidden size and epsilon, pre-splitting 1/hidden_size and eps into FP32 hi/lo constants.

nodes.s: Six small Ascend kernels that carry the speculative-decoding verification bookkeeping: building per-row verification metadata, broadcasting per-request sampling params to query rows, top-k lookups and remapping, accept/reject resolution and the final output assembly.

k.s: Expands each request's first-token-position and query length into per-row request ids, local step indices and an is_verify mask that the rest of the verification chain indexes by row.
Broadcasts per-request temperature, top-p, top-k, seed and sample position onto every query row, offsetting the position by the local step so each speculative step draws independently.
Looks a query id up in a per-row key/value table (by key or by index) and returns the matching value, or -inf / -1 when the key is absent — used to score a chosen token against the draft top-k.
Realigns the draft model's top-k indices and log-probs from the draft pool rows onto the target model's row layout, producing aligned log-probs and the draft token's local index.
Resolves per-row acceptance: walks back over the earlier rows of the same request so a row counts as accepted only if every preceding speculative step was, and marks the first rejected row final.
Assembles the verification output — accepted token ids, per-request accept counts, optional confidence and top-logprobs, and stop-token detection — in one kernel.

nodes.s: Ascend paged KV-cache store with register-side quantization: BF16 rows are quantized to FP8/FP4 with their scales into one aligned UB row and written out by a single exact-length DMA per row or run.

k.s: JIT factory for the store kernel, specialized on the KVCacheFormat layout and block size; handles plain BF16 copies, packed main-cache rows with trailing scales, and page-wide index-cache value/scale sections, skipping slot -1.

nodes.s: Backend-neutral constants and small helpers shared by every TileLang operator: FP4/FP8 range and margin constants, power-of-two and alignment helpers, and the draft-sampling constants DRAFT_POS_HASH_MUL and DRAFT_PROB_PENALTY.

k.s: Computes the largest finite magnitude, exponent bias and maximum exponent for an arbitrary exponent/mantissa split, so quantization code can derive FP8/FP4 ranges instead of hard-coding them.

nodes.s: CUDA (SM100) twin of the fused sampling kernel: one pass over the logits does temperature-softmax, a radix-histogram top-p/top-k threshold search and plain or reject sampling, on top of the two-level sampler primitives in the sibling random_sampling module.

k.s: JIT factory for the CUDA fused sampling kernel, specialized on vocab_size and the do_sample / do_reject_sampling switches; picks thread and block-dim tiling by vocab size and emits softmax, radix threshold search, masking, sampling and the reject-sampling retr

nodes.s: CUDA megakernel running the optional RMSNorm to RoPE to Hadamard to FP8/FP4 cast to KV-cache-store pipeline in one launch, so the post-projection transform touches hidden states only once.

k.s: Builds the fused norm / RoPE / Hadamard / quantize / store kernel from the stage switches, rotary geometry (neox vs interleaved, offset, conjugate), cast format and scale-factor layout, and the target KVCacheFormat.

nodes.s: CUDA RMSNorm kernel with optional residual add, output scaling and fused FP8 cast; emits per-channel scale factors in plain, packed-ue8m0 or TMA-aligned column-major form for the downstream DeepGEMM call.

k.s: JIT factory for the CUDA RMSNorm kernel, specialized on hidden size, dtypes, residual/FP8 switches, scale-factor layout and all sequence-direction strides.

nodes.s: Nine-line CUDA quantization helper exposing the ue8m0 exponent rounding used by norm, fused_transform and store_kv_cache.

k.s: Rounds a scale up to a power of two by bit-manipulating its FP32 exponent, returning -ceil(log2(scale)) — the exponent of the 2^exp quantization multiplier whose ue8m0 dequant byte is -exp + 127.

nodes.s: Two-level fixed-point weighted sampler for CUDA: one CTA per row folds the row into BD per-lane sums, a coarse search picks the lane and a fine search resolves the exact column. Shared by the standalone sampling kernel and by fused_sample.

k.s: Frozen dataclass holding the compile-time sampling layout (vocab_size, threads, lane width bd and fixed-point scale) plus the derived chunk and slot counts.
Converts a probability in [0, 1] to floor(x * 2**scale_bits) exactly from the FP32 mantissa and exponent bits, guarding against the undefined shift of 64 or more.
Block-wide inclusive integer scan built from warp-level segments plus a cross-warp carry pass, optionally reversed.
Folds one chunk of probabilities into the per-lane fixed-point accumulators acc_frag[k] = sum_m probs[row, k + m*BD].
Coarse level: draws one 64-bit uniform target in [0, total) and locates the BD-lane offset it falls into, publishing the remainder and the total mass for the fine pass.
Fine level: casts the gathered arithmetic-sequence probabilities to fixed point, scans them and maps the slot the remainder lands in back to the absolute column k0 + m*BD.
JIT factory for the standalone CUDA sampler — one CTA per row, two-level weighted sampling — specialized on vocab_size and the next-n (MTP) predictor path.

nodes.s: Six small CUDA kernels carrying the speculative-decoding verification bookkeeping: per-row verification metadata, broadcasting per-request sampling params, top-k lookup and remapping, accept/reject resolution and the final output assembly.

k.s: Expands each request's first-token-position and query length into per-row request ids, local step indices and an is_verify mask indexed by row.

Broadcasts per-request temperature, top-p, top-k, seed and sample position onto every query row, offsetting the position by local_step * DRAFT_POS_HASH_MUL so each speculative step draws independently.
Looks a query id up in a per-row key/value table, either by scanning the keys or by direct indexing, returning -inf / -1 when out of range — used to score a chosen token against the draft top-k.
Realigns the draft model's top-k indices and log-probs from draft pool rows onto the target model's row layout, emitting aligned log-probs, the draft token's local index and identity rows.

Resolves per-row acceptance: a row counts as accepted only if every preceding speculative step of the same request was accepted, and the first rejected row is flagged final; with has_golden it compares against the golden token instead of the raw accept flag.

Assembles the verification output — accepted token ids, per-request accept counts, optional confidence error and top-logprobs, and stop-token detection — in one kernel, spreading each row across the whole CTA to cut serial top-k iterations.

nodes.s: CUDA paged KV-cache store specialized by logical cache layout: copies BF16 rows or quantizes them to FP8/FP4 with ue8m0 scales into the paged cache slots, skipping invalid slots.

k.s: Turns per-group BF16 amax values into FP8 quantization multipliers and their ue8m0 dequant scale bytes.
JIT factory for the paged-cache store kernel, specialized on the KVCacheFormat layout, block size and the FP4 value/scale strides; asserts the layout is pure BF16, pure FP8 or pure FP4.

nodes.s: Defines the single typed return contract of a causal-LM forward pass: the hidden states that feed lm_head, with helpers to trim CUDA-graph padding and to copy into a preallocated output buffer.

k.s: Frozen slotted dataclass holding hidden_states [num_tokens, hidden_size] (the lm_head input); narrow() returns a view trimmed to the real token count after a padded CUDA-graph replay, and copy_() writes another output into this one's preallocated storage.

k.s: nn.Module that adopts (does not rebuild) the HF visual_encoder and aligner: rgb_pad_to_patches turns worker-forwarded raw RGB bytes into normalized patches, the ViT plus batch_downsample and the aligner projection produce one embedding per IMAGE token, and rep

nodes.s: Single source of truth for the image special-token ids (offsets added to vocab_size) and for the mm_token_type wire format shared by the VE processors, the MoE gate and the replace_input_embeds kernel.

k.s: IntEnum of image special-token offsets relative to vocab_size (IMAGE_START, IMAGE_PAD, IMAGE, IMAGE_NEW_LINE, IMAGE_END); the real token id is vocab_size + offset and NUM_SPECIAL bounds the validity check.

IntEnum of per-token modality tags carried in the mm_token_type tensor; values are a fixed wire format because the MoE gate treats anything >= IMAGE as image-class and the replace_input_embeds kernel dispatches on the exact value.

nodes.s: Declares the segment contract between the engine and the VE processors — the per-modality input dataclasses, the processor base class — and the tensor_dict merge that concatenates every processor's output into one sample-level dict.

k.s: Empty dataclass that roots the segment-input hierarchy, letting MMProcessor route a heterogeneous segment list by concrete type.
Image segment: declared width and height plus the optional encoded binary, which is stripped when the image's tokens are already covered by the KV cache.
Text segment carrying only a token count — the token ids themselves stay on the engine side in input_ids, so the VE never sees prompt text.
One request's ordered segment list plus its meta dict (notably image_spans, the per-image token start and length used for cache-prefix splitting and chunk slicing).
Abstract per-modality processor: process() maps one BaseInput segment to a tensor dict; implemented by TextTokenProcessor and ImageProcessorAnyRes.
Merges per-segment tensor dicts into one: the images list is chained in segment order while every other same-named tensor is concatenated along dim 0, so the sample-level keys stay in prompt order.

nodes.s: Anyres image geometry planner and processor: resolves any input resolution into a patch-aligned size under a hard per-image token budget, emits the matching mm_token_type layout and ViT position ids, and defers pad/normalize to the GPU kernel by handing downstream only lazily loaded uint8 pixels.

k.s: Decodes encoded image bytes into a fully loaded RGB PIL image.
Holds the per-channel normalize mean and std that the GPU rgb_pad_to_patches kernel needs; the model derives its scalar constants from this at load time.
One-shot lazy loader that defers decoding and resizing an image until the worker actually needs the tensor, so long multi-image prompts do not hold every decoded image in memory at once.
NamedTuple wrapping the CPU contain-resized HWC uint8 pixels; padding and normalization are left to the GPU rgb_pad_to_patches kernel.
Flattens one sample's ResizedImage pixels into a single raw RGB byte tensor and records each image's actual (width, height) for the GPU patch kernel.
NamedTuple of the complete per-image geometry: patch-aligned pixel size, ViT patch grid, post-downsample LLM grid, and the resulting expanded token count.
Token cost of one image segment: n_llm_h rows of n_llm_w IMAGE tokens each followed by an IMAGE_NEW_LINE, plus the IMAGE_START and IMAGE_END pair.
Batched patch count after downsampling, ceiling-dividing the ViT width and height grids independently so it matches the per-image layout math.
Derives the full ImageLayout (ViT grid, LLM grid, token count) from a patch-aligned pixel size.

Solves for the largest aspect-preserving LLM grid that fits the token budget by combining h/w = aspect ratio with h*(w+1) = max_n_token - 2, with dedicated branches clamping degenerate aspect ratios to a grid of one.
Guard around the naive patch-aligned layout: if it overshoots max_n_token it falls back to solve_resize_ratio, then asserts the token budget actually holds.

Full planner from raw image size to ImageLayout: clamps over-wide images to max_wh_ratio (which switches that image to a stretch resize), upscales below min_pixels, rounds up to patch multiples, then enforces the token budget via safe_resize.

Memoized pure planner that turns an image size into everything the engine needs without touching pixels: token count, patch-aligned target size, images_spatial_crop, scanline-ordered ViT position ids, and the IMAGE_START / IMAGE / IMAGE_NEW_LINE / IMAGE_END mm

BaseProcessor for arbitrary-resolution images: process() plans the layout, returns a lazy ImageTensorLoader plus the spatial-crop, position-id and mm_token_type tensors, while estimate_num_tokens() prices an image for the scheduler without decoding it.

nodes.s: Modality router that converts a request's segment list into one tensor dict by dispatching each segment to its per-modality processor and merging the results.

k.s: Maps segment dataclass type to processor (TextLengthInput to the text processor, ImageInput to the image processor) and seeds the merge with an empty mm_token_type tensor so a zero-segment or fully cached prompt still yields a stable key set.

nodes.s: Text-segment processor for the VE pipeline: a text segment contributes only its length, since the token ids live on the engine side.

k.s: Emits a run of UNDEFINED (0) mm_token_type entries as long as the text segment, producing no token content of its own.

Rewrites every known image placeholder spelling in a prompt to the token string this particular model uses.
Reads local sample images, pairs each prompt with its image bytes and declared sizes, and returns the prompt list plus matching multi_modal_data.
Builds the fixed offline-inference sample set (text-only, single-image and multi-image prompts, replicated per data-parallel rank) with per-sequence sampling params.
Pads each prompt with filler context so that, after image placeholders expand to their real token counts, every sample lands on exactly OFFLINE_INPUT_LEN while keeping BOS first.
Builds the sampling pool of ordinary vocabulary ids by excluding the tokenizer's added special tokens.
Generates a random-pixel 24-bit BMP of the requested size, cheap to encode so image synthesis stays linear in pixel count.
Frozen parameter set for random VL prompt construction — image token id, ViT patch geometry, token budget and the text sampling pool — built from a live LLM via from_llm.

Synthesizes a random image-text prompt whose expanded length is exactly prompt_length: it interleaves images and random text within caller-specified regions that no image may straddle, fills region capacity back to front, and pads each region's remainder with

nodes.s: Unit tests for MultimodalProcessor.overwrite_prompt: checks that image placeholders expand to the right token runs and segment lists across adjacent, leading, text-only and budget-overflow cases, and that image binaries are stripped only when the image is fully KV-cached.

k.s: Builds a worker-free MultimodalProcessor whose per-image token count comes from a (width, height) lookup table instead of the real estimator.
Reduces a segment list to a comparable tuple spec: text segments by length, image segments by width, height and whether the binary was stripped.
Asserts that two image placeholders expand into their declared token runs and that the resulting segments alternate text and image in prompt order.
Asserts a prompt with no images passes through unchanged and yields a single text segment.
Covers the boundary cases of an image at position zero and two images back to back, where no text segment separates them.
Asserts a placeholder that would exceed the budget is left as a plain text token rather than expanded.
Asserts that declaring image sizes without supplying bytes still expands the placeholders and produces image segments with no binary.
Asserts an image whose tokens are entirely covered by the prefix cache has its binary dropped, so the VE never decodes it.
Asserts a only partially cached image keeps its binary, since its uncached tokens still need real pixels.

Splits the flat prompt-logprob vector back into per-request lists, returning None for requests that did not ask for prompt logprobs and an empty list when the values were never materialized.

Computes one chunk of prompt logprobs: logits GEMM, optional force-topk narrowing, fused_sample for the transformed logprobs, then a map_lookup of each prompt token's logprob. Returns None on non-zero context-parallel ranks, which only join the collective.

Drives `_compute_prompt_logprobs_chunk` over 8192-row chunks so the logits tensor stays bounded; only CP rank 0 allocates the result, but every rank must see the same row count to keep chunk boundaries aligned.

The one entry to logits post-processing: expands per-request temperature / top-p / top-k / seed to packed rows, optionally narrows to force_topk, realigns the previous step's draft top-k into the fresh top-k space, then runs fused_sample, which returns logprob

nodes.s: Wrapper + PyTorch reference + pytest layer for the six TileLang sampling/verification ops (prepare_verification_metadata, expand_sampling_params, map_lookup, remap_draft_topk, get_accept_result, finalize_verification). Each wrapper allocates outputs and dispatches through `ops.*_tl`, which picks the cuda/ or asc/ backend; the `*_ref` twins define the semantics the tests hold both backends to. No dense math here — this is index prep, gathers and verification bookkeeping.

PyTorch oracle for prepare_verification_metadata, built from repeat_interleave and arange; the tests check the TileLang kernel against it.
Dispatches the TileLang kernel that turns (ftp, seqlen_q) into per-row request id, request-local step and an is_verify mask that is false only on each request's final fresh-sampling row.
PyTorch oracle for expand_sampling_params, indexing the per-request parameter tensors by row_to_req.

PyTorch oracle for map_lookup covering both the by_key search and the by_index gather, including the -inf / -1 out-of-range conventions.

Dispatches the TileLang row-wise lookup kernel: `by_key` searches each row's key vector for the queried token id, `by_index` gathers a column directly. Missing keys yield -inf (or -1 for integer values), which is what makes force-topk logprob lookups safe when

PyTorch oracle for remap_draft_topk, scattering the draft top-k into a dense row before gathering it back through the target top-k index.
PyTorch oracle for get_accept_result, reproducing the golden override and prefix-acceptance rules on CPU-side tensors.

Dispatches the TileLang kernel that turns raw per-row rejection decisions into a per-request accepted prefix: it applies golden-token overrides, cuts acceptance at the first mismatch, and marks each request's first rejected (or fresh) row as final.
PyTorch oracle for finalize_verification, assembling every counter and payload the fused kernel produces so the test can compare them field by field.

Reference for the confidence-error term folded into finalize_verification: the summed absolute gap between the kernel's acceptance probability and the draft's self-reported confidence over verification rows.
Checks the metadata kernel against its reference over random per-request query lengths, so both fresh-only and speculative requests are covered.
Checks that expanded per-row sampling parameters match the reference, including the uint64 seed round-trip and the hashed sample position.
Parametrized correctness test for map_lookup across both modes, several value dtypes and missing-key rows.
Checks that draft top-k logprobs and ids realigned into the target top-k space match the dense reference.
Checks prefix acceptance and golden-token override handling, asserting exactly one final row per request.

Times the map_lookup kernel across modes and value dtypes through the benchmark fixtures.
Times remap_draft_topk at representative total_q and force_topk sizes.

Times the sampling-parameter expansion kernel across request counts and speculative step counts.

The optional `ftp` argument lets one per-request bitmask address the correct packed row for a given speculative step.

PyTorch oracle for the bitmask kernel: unpacks the 32-bit words per row and masked_fills the disallowed columns, skipping requests whose step row falls past their query length.
Checks the direct-addressing path (no ftp) against the reference for several logits dtypes.
Checks the ftp path, where each request's bitmask must land on the packed row for the given speculative step and out-of-range steps must be skipped.
Times the direct-addressing bitmask kernel across batch sizes and reports the bytes it touches.
Times the ftp bitmask kernel across request counts and reports the bytes it touches.

Driver-side verification results handed to MTP decode: each request's accepted draft count, the golden token that seeds the next drafts, and the MTPSamplingInput used to sample them.
Per-rank input to MTP decode: the first packed row of each request (-1 marks CUDA graph padding) plus the optional driver payload; follower ranks receive the driver results inside the model instead.

Single packaging-and-tooling config for the deepinfer 0.1.0 distribution: a setuptools build backend requiring ninja and torch >= 2.7, Apache-2.0 metadata pinned to Python >= 3.12 with dependencies left dynamic (resolved from the requirements-*.txt chain), the pytest marker vocabulary (ci, ci_npu, benchmark, long_context, gpu) with testpaths=tests, and a ruff lint profile (E/F/UP/B/SIM/I/ANN/TID251, line-length 140, vendor/ excluded).

Base runtime dependency manifest, fully version-pinned (21 packages). Beyond the usual transformers/tokenizers/safetensors/numpy stack it pins the two kernel-layer dependencies that define this engine's execution plane — tilelang 0.1.15, which compiles the TileLang ops under model_executor/layers/tilelang_ops, and tile-kernels 2.1.0, the prebuilt TileKernels library — plus xgrammar 0.2.2 for structured outputs and pyzmq/posix_ipc for inter-process control.

Development/CI dependency layer that includes requirements.txt and adds the toolchain the contributor workflow needs: clang-format and ruff for the two formatters, pytest plus pytest-xdist and execnet for the suite, pybind11-stubgen and tree-sitter for stub generation, matplotlib for the sweep Pareto plots, and fastapi/uvicorn for the engine's runtime profiling HTTP server.

NVIDIA-side dependency overlay installed by build.sh when DEEPINFER_ACCELERATOR=nvidia: includes requirements-dev.txt, then adds the CUDA 13.2 PyTorch wheel (torch 2.13.0+cu132, pulled from the cu132 download.pytorch.org find-links index) and flash-attn-4 4.0.0b34.

Huawei Ascend dependency overlay installed by build.sh when DEEPINFER_ACCELERATOR=ascend: includes requirements-dev.txt, then pins the CPU PyTorch build (torch 2.13.0+cpu) paired with torch-npu 2.13.0rc1, which supplies the NPU device backend.

Build/clean driver for the DeepInfer C++ extension: runs `python setup.py build` into an accelerator-tagged build tree, symlinks the resulting `.so` files into `deepinfer/_so/<accelerator>-<arch>/`, and byte-compiles the package. Dispatches on a single `build`/`clean` argument and derives its platform tag from `DEEPINFER_ACCELERATOR` (nvidia or ascend), so the same script produces either the SM100 or the Ascend 950 extension.

k.s: Implements the `build` command: sets `MAX_JOBS` (default 16), runs `setup.py build` into the accelerator-tagged build base, symlinks every produced `.so` into `deepinfer/_so/<platform-tag>/`, hard-fails if nothing was linked, and byte-compiles the `deepinfer`
Implements the `clean` command: removes the accelerator-tagged build base and `_so` link directory, deletes stray `deepinfer/*.so`, and prunes every `__pycache__` directory in the tree.

Wheels land in an accelerator-tagged `vendor-wheels` dir and are installed with `--no-deps --no-index`.

nodes.s: clang-format runner for the `csrc/` C++/CUDA tree, covering `.cpp/.cc/.h/.hpp/.cu/.cuh`. Resolves the clang-format binary from `$CLANG_FORMAT`, then `PATH`, then the pip `clang_format` package, and runs either in-place formatting or a `--check` dry-run that reports each offending file and exits non-zero — the form used by CI and the `make format` target.

k.s: Locates a usable clang-format binary by trying `$CLANG_FORMAT`, then `PATH`, then the executable shipped inside the pip `clang_format` package, and exits with an actionable error if none is found.

nodes.s: Regenerates the `deepinfer/_C/*.pyi` type stubs for the pybind11 extension by running `pybind11_stubgen` against `deepinfer._C`, preloading CUDA's `libcuda.so` stub so the import succeeds on machines without a driver. Finishes by rewriting `typing.Sequence` to bare `Sequence` in the generated `engine.pyi`.

LLVM-based clang-format profile for the C++ side of the engine (csrc/): 4-space indent, attached braces, right-aligned pointers, a 140-column limit and preserved include blocks. Applies to the pybind layer and the C++ scheduler/sequence code, not to the Python engine.

Pins the six DeepSeek vendor submodules the engine delegates its dense math and communication to: DeepGEMM and DeepGEMM-Ascend (GEMM), FlashMLA (attention), DeepEP and DeepEP-Ascend (expert-parallel and Engram all-to-all), and DeepSelect. The CUDA/Ascend pairing here is the clearest statement that DeepInfer targets both SM100 and Ascend 950.
Empty package marker for deep_cluster, the cluster-side helper package (hardware/ and topology/ subpackages) that sits beside the deepinfer engine package rather than inside it.
Empty package marker for deepinfer.distributed, the fully vLLM-derived distributed layer (process-group setup and collective wrappers); exports nothing itself.
Empty package marker for deepinfer.engine, the control-plane package (~58% vLLM-derived) holding the Python engine loop that drives the C++ scheduler; exports nothing itself.
Empty package marker for deepinfer.entrypoints, the 100% vLLM-derived entrypoint package (offline LLM-style API); exports nothing itself.

Type-stub barrel for the compiled deepinfer._C pybind extension, re-exporting its three submodules: cuda_utils (raw driver allocation and IPC), engine (the C++ scheduler/sequence/prepare layer) and graph_timer (CUDA-graph event timing).

Type stub for the _C.cuda_utils pybind module: three functions that allocate device memory with cuMemAlloc directly — bypassing torch's caching allocator — and export/import that memory as a CUDA IPC handle, the mechanism behind cross-process tensor sharing.

k.s: Allocates a 1D byte tensor via a direct cuMemAlloc call, deliberately bypassing torch's caching allocator so the pointer is stable and IPC-exportable.
Turns a pointer previously returned by alloc_tensor into an opaque CUDA IPC handle (bytes) that another process can map.
Maps a CUDA IPC memory handle produced by export_ipc_tensor back into this process as a torch tensor.

nodes.s: Generated type stub for deepinfer._C.engine — the full Python-visible surface of the C++ control plane built from csrc/engine/. It declares 21 classes and 13 free functions covering the continuous-batching Scheduler, the Sequence/SequenceMetadata object model and pools, the BlockManager, every sampler input struct, and the prepare_prompt_v4 / prepare_decode_v4 / *_zos metadata builders. This stub, not any Python module, is the authoritative description of what DeepSeek moved out of vLLM's Python scheduler and into C++.

k.s: Free-list allocator for KV-cache blocks: allocate_nolock hands out block ids, pin_blocks/unpin_blocks protect prefix-cached blocks from reuse, and an explicit lock/unlock pair guards the list when the engine thread and a background thread both touch it.
Decode-step slice of the sampler inputs: MTP first-token positions and per-sequence q lengths, the two tensors the sampler needs to locate each speculative draft's logits row.
Driver-rank sampler bundle grouping the kernel inputs with the prefill and speculative sub-structs, the golden-output tensor and max_top_logprobs; only the driver rank populates it.

Cost model the scheduler uses to price a candidate batch: calc_flops returns (attention_flops, total_flops) from the scheduled q/k lengths, is YOCO-aware via yoco_mode and keep_tokens, and deliberately excludes draft-model work.
Per-request temperature, top-p and top-k tensors handed to the logits transform before sampling.
Prefill-only sampler slice: EOS suppression rows, the EOS token ids and the prompt-logprob request, none of which apply on decode steps.

Mutable argument object threaded into prepare_prompt_v4 / prepare_decode_v4: the sequence metadata list plus the full geometry of a step — block_size and swa_block_size, window_size, dense and sparse compress ratios, max_num_blocks, CP size, Engram max_ngram_s
Carrier for prompt-logprob computation: the enable flag, the logits slab, per-sequence prompt-logprob lengths and the prompt tokens to score.

Per-request result record returned to the engine each step — sampled token and its logprob, optional top-k ids/logprobs and sum_smaller_probs, prompt logprobs, the speculative accept/draft token counts and confidence score, finish reason and finished flag. All
Object pool for RequestOutput records; release() returns a batch of them so the per-step output path does not allocate.
Top-level sampler input struct: the decode and driver sub-bundles plus the selected prompt and token indices that map batch rows onto logits rows.
The three tensors the sampling kernel itself consumes: the logits slab, the per-row sample positions and the per-sequence RNG seeds that make sampling reproducible.

The C++ continuous-batching scheduler — DeepSeek's replacement for vLLM's Python scheduler. It owns the waiting and running queues, admits sequences through try_allocate_seq, emits one step via schedule(SequenceMetadataPool), commits results via process_output

One step's scheduling decision: the scheduled sequences, batched-token and cached-token counts, min/max seqlen_k, the attention and total TFLOPs estimate, the finished sequences, and the clone_states / clone_blocks / zero_states edit lists the worker must appl

Plain token-id container behind Sequence.data and Sequence.compressed_data, exposing length and last-token accessors.

Per-step, pool-allocated view of a scheduled sequence handed to the model runner: seqlen_q / seqlen_k, full_len, prompt vs decode flags, is_last_prompt_chunk, placeholder marker, the last accepted and next-n tokens, sampling params and the structured-output ma
Object pool that hands SequenceMetadata to Scheduler.schedule and takes them back through release(), keeping the per-step metadata path allocation-free.

pybind enum for a sequence's lifecycle: WAITING, RUNNING, SWAPPED and seven terminal states including FINISHED_PREEMPTED and the DeepInfer-specific FINISHED_SO_FAILED (structured output) and FINISHED_VE_FAILED (vision encoder).
Speculative-decoding slice of the sampler inputs: the next-n draft tokens, the MTP info read rows and write slots, and the stop token ids used to cut an accepted run short.
pybind enum selecting how YOCO prefill truncates the kept prefix — OFF, MASK (keep the rows, mask them) or COMPACT (physically drop them).

Assembles the step's RequestOutput records from the raw sampler tensors — sampled ids and logprobs, optional top-k and sum_smaller_probs, the accepted/speculative variants of each, prompt logprobs and first-token positions — drawing the records from a RequestO

Applies SchedulerOutputs' edit lists on the current stream: clones state and block pairs for forked sequences and zeroes the state slots the scheduler marked. Returns the to-release id arrays as zero-copy views over process-static buffers that the next call ov

Engram compression map applied on the host: a token id inside the lookup table becomes its table entry, anything out of range (including negatives) becomes the sentinel. This is what fills Sequence.compressed_data.

nodes.s: Type stub for the _C.graph_timer pybind module: handles for CUDA events, for the event-record nodes inside a captured graph, and for the graph itself. It is how DeepInfer times individual regions of a replayed CUDA graph, where ordinary host-side timing is blind.

k.s: Reference-counted handle to a timing event: record it on a stream, query or synchronize on it, and measure elapsed_time against a later event. Equality and hashing compare the underlying event.
Handle to an event-record node inside a captured graph; get_event/set_event swap which EventHandle the node records into, so a replayed graph can be re-timed without recapture.
Handle to a captured graph whose get_event_record_nodes enumerates the event-record nodes inside it — the entry point for instrumenting a graph after capture.

nodes.s: Factory that turns a V4.1 Hugging Face config.json into the rl_mm_processor_20260707 image preprocessing pipeline. It reads the geometry HF owns (patch_size, downsample_ratio, max_image_tokens, min_pixels, max_wh_ratio, image_token_id) and supplies the two settings HF has no key for — RGB mean/std 0.5 and bf16 output — so model-side baked normalization and worker-side preprocessing cannot drift apart.

k.s: Reads config.json, rejects anything whose model_type is not deepseek_v41, and returns the processor settings dict — validating that every integer geometry field is a positive int and that max_wh_ratio is null or >= 1. The strict `type(x) is not int` check also

nodes.s: Empty package marker for deepinfer.model_executor.layers, the parent of tilelang_ops — the execution plane that is almost entirely DeepSeek-original rather than vLLM-derived.

Empty package marker for the Ascend TileLang backend. It stays empty on purpose: ops.py discovers this package with pkgutil.iter_modules and hoists every `*_tl` factory out of each module, so declaring re-exports here would only create symbol collisions.

Ascend TileLang kernels for the sparse-attention indexer's block-candidate stage: block-max pooling of per-token scores, the compact length of a selected candidate set, and the in-place restore from compact indices back to absolute token indices. The first kernel runs a two-phase design — a prep kernel that builds a packed uint64 work queue with an inter-core prefix sum, then a persistent worker kernel that drains it — so rows of wildly different lengths still balance across vector cores.

k.s: Reduces a [num_rows, max_model_len] bf16 logits slab to one max score per block of 8 or 16 keys, capping at the largest finite bf16 and forcing +inf on each row's last valid block so selection always keeps it. A prep kernel first counts 16K-token tasks per row

Given each row's selected candidate block ids and its valid length, sums how many real tokens those blocks cover — clamping the last partial block — to produce the compact length the indexer then gathers into. Vectorized 64 lanes at a time with a predicated SI

Maps compact indices (positions within the selected candidate blocks) back to absolute token indices in place: block_id = candidate_blocks[index >> block_bits], restored = block_id * block_size + remainder, plus an optional per-row offset. Out-of-range or nega

Each compresses a window of COMPRESS_RATIO fp32 (score, latent) rows into one bf16 kv_compressed row while carrying the window remainder forward through state_cache, so a chunked prefill resumes exactly where the previous chunk stopped.

k.s: Fuses the whole confidence head into one pass: concatenates the hidden state with the optional Markov embedding, takes a dot product against a single weight vector in fp32 (SIMD multiply-accumulate over 64-lane slices, four rows at a time), divides by the temp

It carries two hand-tuned implementations and picks between them at JIT time on row width, which is the clearest example in this backend of TileLang being used for memory movement rather than math.

Engram keys each token by the n-gram ending at it, so the window has to be re-stitched once the previous step's sampled and predicted tokens are known — doing it in a kernel is what removes the host round-trip from the decode loop.
